items.title: 22 injured as Sprinter bus overturns at Sege after tyre burst
items.description: About 22 people were injured in a road accident at Sege after a Sprinter bus suffered a tyre burst and overturned on Friday, October 09, 2026. The accident occurred at about 1130 hours and drew personnel from the Ghana Police Service, the Ghana National Fire Service and residents to the scene. An eyewitness, Mr Evans Doetse Huago, told the Ghana News Agency (GNA) that the vehicle, with registration number GW 569-26, was travelling from Aflao to Accra when its left rear tyre burst. He said the driver lost control of the vehicle, which veered off its course and overturned, injuring the occupants, including the driver. Mr Huago said the language spoken by some of the passengers suggested that they might have been travelling from the Volta Region. He said the injured persons were transported to the Sege Polyclinic for treatment with the assistance of police and fire service personnel. According to him, the vehicle was heavily loaded, with goods packed in both the boot and on the roof, raising concerns about excessive pressure on the tyres. Mr Huago said a welder operating near the accident scene quickly arrived with a tipper truck to assist in transporting the goods to safety, while the police arranged for the removal of the damaged vehicle. Officials at the scene declined to comment to the media at the time of filing this report.

items.title: UN housing expert urges Ghana to strengthen Rent Control Department amid housing affordability concerns
items.description: The United Nations (UN) Special Rapporteur on the right to adequate housing has advised Ghana to support its Rent Control Department with the requisite logistics to boost operations. Koldo Casla said the Government should also ensure that all relevant institutional mechanisms were strengthened for effective monitoring to curb arbitrary rent increases that did not bode well for tenants. A statement copied to the Ghana News Agency by the UN Special Rapporteur at the weekend observed that unaffordability of formally built housing had left many Ghanaians with no choice but to find their way into informal settlements. The statement, which highlighted his conclusion of a 12-day official visit to Ghana, said: “During the visit, I observed the housing construction and physical transformations taking place primarily in Accra.” “I could see flashy billboards around the capital promoting real estate investments at stratospheric prices far from the reach of the average Ghanaian.” The statement said it was important the authorities realised that general unaffordability of formally built housing had left many Ghanaians with no choice but to find their way into informal settlements. “About 31 per cent of the urban population lives in informal settlements,” it said, adding that a considerable number of the citizens were also homeless. The statement encouraged the authorities to actively listen to the needs of people living in poverty in the design of public policies regarding housing. “Construction is one of the leading industries and fastest growing sectors in Ghana, employing hundreds of thousands of people, with an estimated contribution ranging between seven and 15 per cent of the country’s Gross Domestic Product,” it said.

items.title: Delta-BCI partnership reaches 166,000 people with breast cancer education
items.description: A decade-long partnership between Delta Air Lines and Breast Care International (BCI) has reached more than 166,000 people with breast cancer education in Ghana, with over 22,500 people screened and nearly 2,100 suspected cases identified. The figures were highlighted as the two organisations marked 10 years of collaboration at the 2026 BCI Walk for the Cure in Mampong, in the Ashanti Region. The programme has also reached more than 70,100 women through targeted rural screening initiatives, as the partners work to improve access to breast cancer information and early detection. The event brought together breast cancer survivors, healthcare professionals, community leaders and thousands of participants under the theme, “Our Walk, Our Fight, Our Future”. Sarah Annan, Operations Service Manager at Delta Air Lines, said the anniversary was an opportunity to build on the partnership’s achievements. “Ten years of partnership with BCI is a milestone we are proud of, but there is still work to do,” she said. She said the participation of survivors, health professionals and community members at the walk demonstrated the importance of collective action in tackling breast cancer. The decision to host this year’s event in Mampong also highlighted efforts to extend awareness and screening beyond Ghana’s major urban centres, particularly to rural communities where access to such services may be limited. Dr Beatrice Wiafe Addai, President and Founder of BCI, said Delta’s support had helped take breast cancer awareness and early detection messages to communities across the country. “We are grateful for a partnership that has helped us reach people who might otherwise have been left out,” she said. She said the priority was to reach more communities, address barriers to early detection and improve access to breast cancer information and screening, regardless of where women lived. Breast cancer awareness campaigns seek to encourage people to understand the disease, recognise possible warning signs and seek medical assessment when necessary. Early detection can improve treatment options and outcomes, although screening does not guarantee that every case will be identified. The 2026 walk also recognised breast cancer survivors and remembered people who have died from the disease, while acknowledging the families and loved ones affected by their loss. As the partnership enters its next decade, Delta and BCI say their focus remains on expanding breast cancer education and screening and encouraging more people to seek timely medical attention.

items.title: Houthi strike on Riyadh airport kills 12; Saudi-led coalition vows 'decisive' response to worst attack on kingdom in a decade
items.description: At least 12 people were killed and more than 300 wounded in an attack on Riyadh’s international airport on Saturday, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade, as the Houthis escalate a campaign they launched this summer. The dead from the third attack this week on the airport included four Saudis, two people from Bangladesh and one person each from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, the Saudi civil aviation authority said. At the latest count, 309 were wounded, officials said. President Donald Trump said Washington was considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis in the conflict, a spillover from the war on Iran that the US and Israel launched in February. Hospitals were flooded with wounded brought by ambulance and helicopter, some in critical condition after the attack, which occurred without warning. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned the Houthi attack on Sunday, reiterating Pakistan’s commitment to Saudi Arabia’s security under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement. The coalition blamed the group for the strike on King Khalid International Airport, describing it as a “full-fledged war crime” that a diplomatic source attributed to a missile. Earlier in the day, authorities had suspended operations at Riyadh’s international airport. The Saudi civil aviation authority had initially confirmed an attack had injured several people at the sprawling King Khalid International Airport, with a diplomatic source attributing it to a missile fired by Yemen’s Houthi rebels. The situation prompted health officials to activate a rare mass call-up of doctors to deal with the “serious emergency”, a medical source said, while foreign embassies warned their citizens to avoid the facility. Houthis have repeatedly targeted the facility, claiming a series of strikes on Thursday that killed three people and damaged a plane, though they did not announce any new attacks on Saturday. Air traffic monitor Flightradar24 said 155 arriving and 161 departing flights had been cancelled, while a total of 222 flights were delayed. At around 6pm local time, Flightradar24 noted that flights bound for the airport were “diverting elsewhere, mainly to Jeddah at the moment”. It later shared a notice to airmen (Notam) for operations suspended till 12am. A witness at the airport reported hearing an explosion while waiting to board a flight, and another said they saw a strike that left people wounded and fleeing in panic. “I was on gate 403” at the domestic terminal, the witness told AFP . “I saw 401 hit, I saw injured [people] in front of my eyes. Everyone was running.” A medical source told AFP that the health ministry had ordered ER doctors to report to hospitals around the capital to treat the wounded on Saturday. “We were told we are dealing with a ‘serious emergency situation’. Injured are being moved to hospitals across Riyadh”, with many in critical condition, the source said. The aviation authority said the number of injured from the attack was still being assessed, adding that airport “operations had been temporarily suspended pending the completion of an assessment of the damage and verification of the safety of the facilities”. The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers after a truce in their long-running war with Yemen’s coalition government unravelled in July. A source at a local hospital said five people were in intensive care there after being wounded at the airport, with “dozens of people injured” in all. A relative of one wounded person said they had been hit in the shoulders and arms by shattered glass. Three witnesses confirmed people being evacuated from the airport. Two doctors told AFP that several pilgrims headed to Makkah had been injured while waiting to board their flight. A diplomatic source briefed on the matter told AFP the airport was hit by “a missile around 3:00pm” (5pm PKT). “Houthis are attacking civilian targets. Riyadh airport is a civilian target,” the source said. ‘War crime’ Coalition spokesman Major General Turki al-Malki described the strike as a “cowardly terrorist attack” against a civilian facility. “The cowardly terrorist attack by the terrorist Houthi militia… which resulted in deaths and injuries among civilian passengers and airport staff, constitutes a full-fledged war crime,” he said in a statement on X. US ‘may’ join Saudi strikes Asked on Saturday whether he had changed his mind about joining Saudi strikes on the group, US President Donald Trump said: “We may.” He said he would be speaking with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, calling what happened in Saudi Arabia “not acceptable”. US media outlets have reported that previous Saudi requests for US military assistance in dealing with the Houthis have been rebuffed. Embassy warnings The Yemen conflict flared back to life after a four-year, UN-brokered truce collapsed, months into a wider Middle Eastern war that has rocked the region and roiled energy supplies and markets. The scale and frequency of the recent strikes targeting Riyadh are unprecedented in the eight months of war in the region. Saudi Arabia leads an international coalition that supports Yemen’s government militarily, and has found itself drawn deeper into its impoverished neighbour’s civil war. Both Riyadh and the Houthis have signalled a willingness to keep fighting rather than pursue diplomacy. The US embassy in Saudi Arabia said it was “aware of attacks” on Riyadh airport on Saturday and called on American citizens to avoid the area. The Canadian, German and Spanish embassies also warned their citizens to avoid the facility. Spain’s embassy, in a message on X, alerted nationals to a “new attack… by the Houthis”. A senior Western diplomat told AFP that several embassies “indicated that they had decided to prohibit their staff’s travel to/from Riyadh Airport over the next week as a prudential step”. Near the airport, passengers carrying luggage could be seen standing on the pavement at a metro station. Yemen fighting Meanwhile, in Yemen, Saudi-led government forces were advancing against the Houthis in areas they captured last month around the Bab al-Mandab strait, military sources told AFP . The Yemeni government last week announced a counter-offensive aimed at retaking all areas held by the Houthis, after the group seized the country’s entire western coastline in a lightning offensive. The Houthis confirmed that government forces had attacked in the Bab al-Mandab area — a key chokepoint for Red Sea oil and cargo shipping — but they claimed to have repelled the assault. Claims by the warring parties have been impossible to independently verify, with the situation moving fast on the ground and access for journalists difficult.

items.title: FO reiterates Pakistan's 'firm and unshakeable' commitment to Saudi Arabia's security after Riyadh attack
items.description: The Foreign Office (FO) on Sunday condemned a fresh wave of Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, reaffirming Pakistan’s “firm and unshakeable” commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, security and stability of the Gulf state under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement. The defence pact , of which Turkiye is also a part, was signed on August 7 and aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them. The statement comes following Saturday’s attack on Riyadh’s international airport, which killed at least 12 people and wounded 309 others. In a post on X, FO said the targeting of a civilian airport constituted “a heinous act of terrorism, a flagrant violation of international law and a grave threat to regional peace and security”. It expressed concern over the casualties resulting from the attack, extending condolences to the bereaved families and wishing a swift recovery to the injured. “The continued targeting of civilian population and critical infrastructure by the Houthi militia is utterly unacceptable and must be condemned unequivocally by the international community,” the statement read. It added: “Such brazen and indiscriminate acts of aggression cannot be justified under any circumstances and must cease immediately.” FO expressed “unwavering” solidarity with the leadership of Saudi Arabia and reiterated its “firm and unshakeable commitment” to Riyadh’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, security and stability in line with the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and the “recent decision” taken by its Strategic, Political and Defence Committee on October 5, in which the member states had agreed to the rapid deployment of military forces and capabilities in the kingdom. FO expressed support for Saudi Arabia’s right to self-defence against all threats and acts of aggression and went on to urge Yemen’s Houthis to cease attacks and the international community to take “a firm and unequivocal stand” against it. “Pakistan will continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, resolute in its commitment to the kingdom’s sovereignty, security and defence.” Shortly before FO, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, in a post on X, also condemned the attack. In his statement, the premier said that targeting civilian and critical infrastructure was “completely unacceptable and [constitutes] a serious threat to regional peace and stability. “Such acts of violence, which are a flagrant violation of international law, must cease immediately.” Expressing solidarity with Riyadh, PM Shehbaz said, “In accordance with the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and the enduring bonds of brotherhood between our two countries, we reaffirm our steadfast commitment to Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and security.” The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen has blamed the group for the strike on King Khalid International Airport, describing it as a “full-fledged war crime” that a diplomatic source attributed to a missile. Houthis have repeatedly targeted the facility, claiming a series of strikes on Thursday that killed three people and damaged a plane, though they did not announce any new attacks on Saturday. The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers after a truce in their long-running war with Yemen’s coalition government unravelled in July. Against this backdrop, Pakistan has repeatedly expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia. On Oct 5, in an emergency meeting of the Makkah pact in Riyadh, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye agreed to the rapid deployment of military forces and capabilities. Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, who was part of Pakistan’s delegation in the meeting, joined Geo News programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Saath’ via telephone the same day and was asked about a possible operational role by Pakistan and Turkiye, to which he said both Turkiye and Pakistan had a “presence in theatre”, but only Saudi troops were involved in combat operations. On September 18, Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said Pakistan would go to “any extent” to defend the Gulf state, adding that Islamabad’s commitment to the kingdom’s security is “unconditional”. Asif has also reaffirmed that Pakistan will “practically and diplomatically” stand by Saudi Arabia against Yemen’s Houthi rebels if the situation escalates. items.title: PM takes notice of student’s suicide over visa fraud
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The death of student Laiba Aijaz on Friday drew the attention of the government, with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif meeting the Islamabad police chief and chief commissioner and directing them to arrest the accused. Sources in the police and Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) told Dawn that the prime minister called Inspector General Mohammad Sohail Chaudhry and Chief Commissioner Islamabad Sohail Ashraf and directed them to apprehend the man accused of defrauding the deceased student. The IG briefed the prime minister on the incident during the meeting. The capital police registered a case against the accused under Sections 322 and 34 of the Pakistan Penal Code on Saturday, following a complaint lodged by Mohammad Aijaz, a native of Sargodha residing in G-10. The accused allegedly defrauded the student of millions of rupees, following which she reportedly took her own life. Orders arrest of accused agent The minister of state for interior and narcotics control also contacted FIA officers and directed them to take strict action against the accused. The FIA Islamabad Zone has initiated an investigation and is conducting raids at various locations to trace and arrest him, according to a statement issued by the agency. The FIA Islamabad Zone director also visited Laiba’s residence, met her family and gathered details about the incident. According to the FIA, the accused allegedly gained the family’s trust by misrepresenting his identity and professional status before obtaining money from them for different purposes. He was not a registered visa agent but claimed to work as an accountant at the Supreme Court of Pakistan. He later made conflicting claims about his identity and employment, the agency said. The FIA statement said Rs550,000 was paid to the accused for securing employment for Laiba’s brother, while Rs7.2 million was handed over to him on the pretext of securing Laiba’s admission to Harvard University in the United States. The agency said the payments and claims made by the accused were being examined and further legal action would follow as the investigation progressed. Laiba had recently completed her BS degree from the International Islamic University Islamabad (IIUI). The accused allegedly defrauded her with the help of a female accomplice. According to a police report, her father contacted the police helpline after she went missing, saying she was under extreme psychological distress. Following an analysis of call detail records and location data, a joint police and family search found her body hanging by a scarf from a tree inside a fenced enclosure on the G-10 Sunday Bazaar green belt. The body was taken to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) in an Edhi ambulance. After the autopsy, the victim’s clothes and biological samples were secured and sealed for forensic examination. The formal autopsy report is awaited. Investigators have secured the visa documents allegedly provided by the accused. A special police team has also been formed to trace and arrest him and his female accomplice. His name has been placed on the stop list to prevent him from leaving the country. Police sources said Laiba’s family had arranged money for the agent by selling a plot and gold ornaments. Published in Dawn, October 11th, 2026

items.title: Broken record: Friendship with Britain and Hindustan
items.description: With the advantage of hindsight, one has the opportunity to study the historical cycles in a nation’s life. Thanks to this newspaper’s unique, extensive archive of back issues, one can examine the major political, economic and social trends that have shaped Pakistan and the world over the last seven decades and counting. Cliched as it may sound, history repeats itself, and we — as a state and as a polity — largely refuse to learn from it. Through this platform, we will look back at the ‘big’ stories that made it to the front pages of Dawn , as well as significant developments tucked away in the inside pages, from the birth of Pakistan onwards, and try to put them in perspective. We will study the critical issues of the week, starting from Aug 14, 1947 and examine the major themes and issues that made it to the paper. Though Dawn ’s archive goes back further, we have chosen to start from the day Pakistan was born. The news items have been selected for their relevance — in the eyes of this writer — to the modern day as well as their historical impact. ‘Friendship with Britain and Hindustan’ The front page of the Dawn Delhi edition of Aug 14, 1947 captured the zeitgeist of the time: a fond farewell to empire, and hope for the future. Quaid-i-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah, while delivering a speech at a state dinner in honour of Lord Louis Mountbatten, the last viceroy of India, spoke of the British warmly, saying Pakistan would “endeavour to create and maintain goodwill and friendship with Britain and our neighbouring dominion — Hindustan. …” Though relations with Britain saw ups and downs, they have remained generally cordial. The same, obviously, cannot be said for India. Mere months after the Quaid would express his desire for good relations with India, both nations went to war over Kashmir, as Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession to India, a process that would spark a dispute that remains unsolved to this day; despite how New Delhi may spin it, Jammu and Kashmir remains a disputed region. Moreover, Pakistan and India have fought numerous major and minor wars, with the last conflict breaking out in May 2025 after the Pahalgam incident. The unfinished business of Partition remains unfinished, and has resulted in a permanent state of hostility between Pakistan and India. A single-column news item on the front page reflected another, forgotten territorial dispute that has now become a part of history. It mentioned that the princely State of Junagadh, in the Kathiawar region of what is now India’s Gujarat state, had decided to join Pakistan. Mr. Ismail Abramani, Secretary for Constitutional Affairs to Junagadh State, “met Mr. Jinnah … and communicated to him the decision of the State.” Interestingly, when the Muslim nawab of Junagadh decided to accede to Pakistan, India did not accept it and occupied the state in November 1947. Yet the Kashmiri Hindu maharaja’s accession to India was perfectly acceptable to New Delhi. The Indian rulers of the time clearly shifted the goalposts when it suited them. Trouble in Lahore But with great hope there was also trepidation. The inside pages carried reports of communal disturbances which reflected the frenzy that accompanied Partition. A grim report from Lahore told the reader that “most of the sectors in the Walled City are on fire and burning unchecked”. It added that the military and police had been “firing incessantly in several places, where arson and looting was rampant”. So volatile was the situation that the district magistrate clamped an 11-hour curfew on many parts of the Punjab capital; three military brigades had to be moved in to control the situation. Disturbances had also been reported from Amritsar (East Punjab) and Moradabad (UP). Though Independence held great promise for the people of the subcontinent, freed as they were from colonial subjugation, as the record shows, the bitter rivalry between the erstwhile dominions of Pakistan and Hindustan has persisted, while communalism remains entrenched on both sides of the border. The pages of Dawn would over the decades tell these — and other — stories that shaped the future of Pakistan, and made it what it is today. It is these stories we will seek to examine every week.

items.title: Économie russe : une entreprise du pays sur trois est déficitaire
items.description: En Russie, 11 secteurs d’activité sur 79 ont affiché un résultat financier négatif au cours de la période janvier-juillet, selon les données de Rosstat. Parmi les secteurs les plus impactés par la dégradation de la situation économique figurent la métallurgie, dont les grandes et moyennes entreprises ont enregistré un solde négatif de 269 milliards de roubles (2,8 milliards d’euros) sur la période, la finance et les assurances (-247 milliards), et l’extraction de charbon (-178 milliards) Кассовое неравенство : число убыточных отраслей бизнеса выросло в четыре раза », Известия , 7 octobre 2026.'> 1 . Après déduction des pertes, le total des bénéfices des grandes et moyennes entreprises russes s’élève à 13 000 milliards de roubles (136 milliards d’euros) sur la période, soit 16 % de moins que l’année précédente. Au total, 43 000 entreprises ont clôturé cette période avec un bénéfice, tandis que 22 000 ont enregistré une perte nette. La part des entreprises déficitaires est ainsi en hausse sur un an, et a atteint 33,4 % – soit 2,8 points de plus que sur la même période de 2025. Les entreprises russes peinent à générer des bénéfices face aux coûts élevés des emprunts et à la hausse des charges. Bien que le taux directeur de la Banque centrale ait été abaissé à 14 % en juillet – soit 7 points de moins par rapport au pic atteint entre octobre 2024 et juin 2025 –, les entreprises font souvent face à des taux d’emprunt qui dépassent les 20 %. Afin de financer la guerre contre l’Ukraine, le Kremlin a fait passer au 1er janvier la TVA de 20 à 22 %, ce qui contribue à l’augmentation des coûts. Dans le même temps, la faible demande rend plus difficile la répercussion de ces hausses sur les prix. Selon un sondage conduit en juin par PSB, une banque russe, 22 % des entreprises déclarent que leur stratégie actuelle est la « survie » . Tous les secteurs ne sont pas impactés par ces conditions économiques défavorables : les entreprises d’extraction de pétrole et de gaz ont vu leurs bénéfices augmenter de 51 % sur la période en raison de la hausse du prix du baril liée au blocage du détroit d’Ormuz, et les entreprises pharmaceutiques (+34 %) ainsi que les industries liées aux commandes de défense. Les entreprises pétrolières russes sont toutefois impactées par les suspensions d’activité prolongées et les opérations de réparation et de maintenance de plus en plus fréquentes imposées par les frappes ukrainiennes. Afin de continuer d’approvisionner le marché intérieur en carburant, le gouvernement russe a versé en septembre la plus importante subvention aux compagnies pétrolières depuis avril 2022 : 305 milliards de roubles, soit 3,2 milliards d’euros. L’article Économie russe : une entreprise du pays sur trois est déficitaire est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: CAN de futsal 2026 : Hicham Dguig, le maître d’œuvre d’une génération dorée
items.description: À l’approche de la Coupe d’Afrique des nations (CAN) de futsal 2026, organisée au Maroc, Hicham Dguig s’apprête à conduire à nouveau les Lions de l’Atlas dans leur quête d’un quatrième sacre continental, avec l’ambition de poursuivre une dynamique qui a permis au futsal marocain de s’imposer parmi les références du continent. À la tête de la sélection nationale depuis plusieurs années, le technicien marocain a accompagné l’essor du futsal national et contribué à l’installation du Maroc au sommet de la hiérarchie africaine. Sous sa conduite, les Lions de l’Atlas ont remporté les CAN de 2016, 2020 et 2024, construisant progressivement un palmarès qui traduit la régularité de la sélection sur la scène continentale. Cette continuité constitue l’un des principaux atouts du Maroc à l’approche de la prochaine échéance. Le groupe a acquis une expérience importante des grandes compétitions et s’appuie sur une identité de jeu construite au fil des années. Pour Hicham Dguig, l’enjeu sera toutefois de maintenir cette dynamique dans une compétition disputée à domicile. Le statut de tenant du titre et la pression liée à l’organisation constituent autant de facteurs auxquels les Lions de l’Atlas devront répondre avec maîtrise. Le sélectionneur pourra notamment compter sur un groupe habitué aux rendez-vous internationaux et sur une nouvelle génération appelée progressivement à prendre davantage de responsabilités au sein de l’équipe nationale. L’objectif demeure clair : conserver le trophée continental et offrir au public marocain un nouveau sacre. Pour y parvenir, le Maroc devra d’abord franchir l’obstacle de la phase de groupes, où il sera opposé à l’Algérie, à la Libye et à la Zambie. Au-delà du résultat sportif, cette CAN s’inscrit dans la continuité d’un projet qui dépasse les seules performances de l’équipe nationale. Le développement de la formation, l’élévation du niveau du championnat national et la multiplication des confrontations internationales ont accompagné la progression du futsal marocain. Avec Hicham Dguig à la barre, les Lions de l’Atlas abordent ainsi cette nouvelle campagne avec l’ambition de confirmer leur domination africaine et de poursuivre leur ascension au plus haut niveau international. The post CAN de futsal 2026 : Hicham Dguig, le maître d’œuvre d’une génération dorée appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

Decenas de personas esperan pacientes su turno para ver al hombre que se ha convertido en la gran esperanza del sector izquierdista de los demócratas . Cuando comienza a hablar estalla la locura: “Mi nombre es Abdul El-Sayed y voy a ser vuestro próximo senador en Washington”. Durante la próxima hora, los centenares de personas que se congregan en este recinto aplaudirán, reirán y jalearán cada palabra que salga de la boca de la nueva estrella de la política estadounidense, que ha convertido ya en marca de la casa su uniforme de camiseta negra ajustada y vaqueros . items.title: Aitana Sánchez-Gijón: “Ya están aquí. Censurando, denunciando, ganando. Y nos lo estamos comiendo”
items.description: El domingo 27 de septiembre, cuando las primeras tiendas de campaña de la madrileña Puerta del Sol no llevaban ni 24 horas levantadas, Aitana Sánchez-Gijón visitó la acampada naciente. Repartió kilos de plátanos y empanadas a los jóvenes que no pensaban moverse de ahí en los próximos días. Saludó a su hijo mayor, el cantante Teo Lucadamo , quien había pernoctado con ellos. Grabó un vídeo para sus redes sociales: “Si estáis por Madrid, en vuestras ciudades, organizaos, acampad y haceos oír. Todas y todos juntos creo que podemos conseguir grandes cosas”, pidió a sus seguidores. Y se fue a trabajar, a Alcalá de Henares, donde esos días representaba la obra Malquerida , actualmente de gira. Mientras actuaba, el vídeo se viralizó y su visita se convirtió en uno de los momentos más comentados de aquel primer día de acampada. Lo que estaba sucediendo en Sol, esa rabia acumulada, no era solo cosa de jóvenes. Seguir leyendo Estilismo: Beatriz Machado Maquillaje y peluquería: Alba Esteban (TEN Agency) Manicura: Lucero Hurtado para OPI Producción: Cristina Serrano Asistentes de fotografía: Maitane Huidobro y Ayub El Kadmiri Asistente de estilismo: Paloma Gutiérrez Asistente de producción: Marina Marco

items.title: Esa cosa tan desprestigiada
items.description: Mientras escribo esto (15 días antes de que se publique, como sabéis), la guerra de las cartas está en lo más álgido. Me refiero al tremendo cirio organizado tras la retirada de la invitación para acudir al Festival Cultur Alh de Granada a la escritora argentina Ariana Harwicz , por sus opiniones sobre Gaza. Leí un artículo suyo titulado “Cómo llegaron a llamar nazis a los judíos”, con el que estoy en total desacuerdo. Cuando se conoció el veto, siete autores publicaron una carta en apoyo de la cancelación, por negar el genocidio y por haber descalificado a los partidarios del pueblo palestino. Enseguida salió otra carta de 350 escritores solidarizándose con Harwicz y rechazando ese tipo de censuras. Y poco después apareció una tercera misiva de más de 500 autores a favor de los siete primeros y de la opción de echar a Ariana. En eso estamos ahora, mientras tecleo: justo en esta inflación acelerada de epístolas furiosas y autores firmantes. No sé cómo continuará esta guerra. Quizá se sigan publicando declaraciones hasta el infinito. A veces pienso que hay más escritores que lectores en el mundo, así que seguro que aún quedan rúbricas por captar. Seguir leyendo

items.title: The pushed river
items.description: THE Indus River is moving east in central Pakistan. Along an 85-kilometre stretch from upstream of Layyah city down to Taunsa Barrage, it is pressing hard against its eastern bank. In this year’s flood season, it destroyed Basti Kanjal, a riverine settlement of more than 500 houses some 15km northwest of Layyah. It did not stop there, washing away several more settlements. Since June, close to 5,000 acres of cultivated land have been lost; according to news reports, 100,000 people have been displaced. A close analysis of 38 years of satellite imagery shows that the river is not wandering. It is being pushed. Ask any elder in the riverside villages of Churkin or Basira which face the Vehowa hill torrent’s mouth 30km upstream of Layyah about the river of his childhood, and he will tell you the Indus was 10 miles (16km) wide. He will also tell you that the river gave as much as it took: land drowned on one bank surfaced on the other, and the patwari’s records followed the water back and forth. The satellites agree with him on the width. Between 1988 and 1997, the active belt below Churkin measured 16km to 18km, and above Taunsa Barrage nearly 24km. Today, it is reduced to a third. A river squeezed into a narrow gut runs deeper and faster, and expends its vigour on eroding vulnerable banks. Three engineering structures, built with public money and international loans, have together hemmed in the river on three sides. The first of these is the Chashma Right Bank Canal, financed by the Asian Development Bank. The canal runs through the Suleiman hill torrents. These are no small streams: the Vehowa alone drains a catchment of over 2,600 square kilometres and has recorded flood peaks above 35,000 cusecs. Before the canal, such floods spread across the Daman plain under the old rod-kohi system, watering the land and dropping their silt on the way. After 2003, the canal’s 68 cross-drainage structures began delivering every flood, with its full load of mountain sediment, to fixed points on the river’s right bank. Between 2011 and 2016, two great fans of new land rose out of the riverbed — one at the Vehowa’s mouth opposite Layyah, and one at the mouth of the Sanghar torrent near Taunsa city. Together, they hold some 37sq km of new permanent land, a metre and more above the old riverbed, and about 100 million cubic metres of sediment. Where the trained torrents deliver their load, walls have risen; in the intervening stretches, the river’s western edge hasn’t moved in 38 years. The canal itself has been closed since the 2022 floods, but its silt walls remain standing in the river. A close analysis of 38 years of satellite imagery shows that the Indus is not wandering. It is being pushed. The second factor is Taunsa Barrage. Built in 1958 to pass a million cusecs, its capacity fell by half within five decades as sediment accumulated. A wedge of silt today stands nearly 2m high near the pond and stretches 40km upstream, flattening the river’s slope and promoting further deposition. The World Bank’s 2005-08 rehabilitation project raised the crest and built a secondary weir downstream. But the embankments were never raised proportionately. Local communities protested and wrote to the Bank that the remodelling ignored the sedimentation, causing flood protection for structures to fail. In 2010, a flood peak of 960,000 cusecs breached the eastern marginal embankment upstream, allowing the river to outflank the structure and carve a new channel. Their warning proved correct. The third factor relates to the embankments. The marginal ones along the left bank, running some 40km from Daira Din Pannah up towards Layyah, froze the river’s eastern edge decades ago, and the floodplain strip between the river and bund has since been almost entirely converted into farms and settlements. In the 1990s, the river still reclaimed that strip in every high flood; today, 95 per cent of it has turned into permanent land. Meanwhile, the restricted riverbed is level with the protected villages outside — all that protects them now is the crest of an earthen bund. This is the fuller picture of the narrative that those affected recounted outside the Layyah Press Club this September, as they blamed two decades of Chashma Canal silt for their plight: sediment walls advancing from the west, a wedge of silt backed up behind the barrage, and, on the east, the embankments holding the door shut. A river so enclosed has nowhere to go but against the weakest point. In 2010, the weakest point was the marginal bund above Taunsa; in 2026, it was the training works at the Layyah bridge. The river has now cut to within 200m of the Lala, its old channel passing along the western edge of Layyah city. The city’s protection bund stops 3.5km short of that point. What happens if the river completes its eastward shift? The low floodplain east of the river holds hundreds of villages built on the assumption that the river would keep to its corridor. A river breaching the Lala line would place Layyah on the front line, and behind it Jaman Shah, Kot Sultan, and Paharpur. An eastward-shifted Indus would progressively outflank Taunsa Barrage itself. A barrage commands only the water that arrives at its gates; the canals of Dera Ghazi Khan and Muzaffargarh, irrigating millions of acres, depend on that command. The river would leave the barrage presiding over a dying channel. The communities of this region warned both lending institutions years ago, the ADB over the canal and the World Bank over the barrage, through formal complaints, inspection claims, and hunger strikes. I was among those who warned. I remember how patiently they were heard and how completely they were ignored. Both institutions noted lessons and closed their files. The river has now reopened them, writing its supplement in drowned villages and 5,000 acres of lost land. Reconstruction without the benefit of an honest analysis of these structural challenges would be tantamount to allowing a similar situation, or even worse, in the future. The analysis now exists, measured from orbit and verifiable by anyone. What remains is whether anyone with authority is willing to read it. The writer is a native of Taunsa and teaches at Quaid-i-Azam University, Islamabad. Published in Dawn, October 11th, 2026

items.title: Cándido Conde-Pumpido: “Cuestionar al Tribunal Constitucional es cuestionar la democracia”
items.description: Cándido Conde-Pumpido (A Coruña, 77 años), presidente del Tribunal Constitucional, ha elaborado la sentencia que pone fin al debate jurídico sobre la aplicación de la ley de amnistía a los líderes del procés . La resolución, aprobada esta semana, cuestiona la interpretación de la norma que hizo el Tribunal Supremo, ordena al alto tribunal que aplique el perdón también al delito de malversación y fija la doctrina constitucional sobre el asunto. La decisión, de trascendencia histórica, abre la puerta a que el expresident Carles Puigdemont pueda regresar a España nueve años después de huir tras el proceso independentista que provocó una profunda fractura política y social en Cataluña y que planteó uno de los mayores desafíos constitucionales a los que se ha enfrentado España desde la Transición. Seguir leyendo

items.title: ¿Juntos o separados? Calcula cómo se moverían los escaños con distintas coaliciones
items.description: ¿Cuánto cambiaría el pronóstico de las encuestas con una coalición a la izquierda del PSOE? A continuación respondemos esa pregunta, y muchas parecidas, simulando cientos de elecciones. Seguir leyendo Metodología Los cálculos parten del modelo de predicción electoral de EL PAÍS que usamos por ejemplo aquí o aquí . El cálculo consiste en tres pasos: 1) Promediamos las encuestas publicadas, dando más peso a las más recientes y a las encuestadoras con mejor historial. 2) Trasladamos ese voto a cada provincia a partir de los resultados de 2023 (y de las europeas de 2024 para los partidos que entonces no se presentaron por separado). 3) Por último, simulamos 20.000 elecciones: en cada una, el voto de cada partido se desvía del promedio tanto como históricamente han fallado las encuestas a esta distancia de las urnas, y se reparten los escaños de las 52 circunscripciones con la fórmula D’Hondt y la barrera del 3%. Los escaños que de cada escenario son la media de sus simulaciones, y la probabilidad de mayoría es el porcentaje de ellas en que PP y Vox suman 176 o más. Para las coaliciones, sumamos en cada simulación los votos de los partidos que se unen y repetimos el reparto. Asumimos como hipótesis que la coalición conserva todos los votos de sus partes, sin perder ni sumar votantes. En el escenario de giro a la izquierda, movemos 3,5 puntos de voto del PP, Vox y Se Acabó la Fiesta a PSOE, Sumar-IU y Podemos, en proporción al tamaño de cada partido. La suma de PP y Vox incluye a UPN.

items.title: Ada Colau, la exalcaldesa que puso la vivienda en la agenda pública ahora quiere dar el salto al Congreso
items.description: No podía ser casualidad. Todo a la vez, en pocas semanas. Un día se sumó a parar un desahucio, la misma semana acudió a manifestaciones, activó cuentas de redes sociales que estaban en silencio, dio entrevistas y participó en tertulias que acabaron siendo noticia. Como el día que explicó que compartirá piso porque no llega a fin de mes . Con el inicio de curso, Ada Colau , la ex alcaldesa de Barcelona, líder indiscutible de los comunes (pese a no tener cargo orgánico) y presidenta de la Fundación Sentit Comú, irrumpió de nuevo en la agenda pública , disparando las preguntas sobre su posible retorno a la vida política. En Cataluña, cuando se habla de Colau y de esta posibilidad, se da por descontado de que hablamos del Congreso de los Diputados; la política catalana nunca ha sido una opción para quien fue ocho años alcaldesa y es una gran defensora del municipalismo. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El movimiento de vivienda señala a los pequeños caseros: ¿son responsables del alza de los precios?
items.description: Iria y Laura son amigas desde la universidad y compañeras de piso desde hace seis años. Al tercer día de protestas por la vivienda, estas jóvenes de 28 años, que prefieren no dar su apellido, se plantaron en la Puerta del Sol de Madrid , donde, quitando algún relevo ocasional, duermen cada noche. Por la mañana acuden al trabajo, una en una clínica de psicología y la otra en una asociación de acompañamiento a menores en riesgo de exclusión. Al cerrar la tienda de campaña, cuelgan una gran cartulina rosa en la que se lee Luego volvemos. Estamos trabajando para nuestro casero . Seguir leyendo

items.title: El gran enfado salta a las urnas
items.description: Inés Caballero charlaba con dos amigas en la acampada de la Puerta del Sol el jueves pasado. Las tres, sentadas en unas sillas de camping , se encontraban en el centro mismo del laberinto de tiendas que abarrotaba la plaza, protegidas, por un mar de plásticos y lonas, de la lluvia, de las miradas y, hoy, del sol. Inés tiene 28 años, es técnico de teatro en Madrid, el trabajo le gusta, estudió para llegar a él, cobra un sueldo de unos 1.500 euros al mes, goza de contrato fijo y sin embargo, acudió a la llamada de acampar en la Puerta del Sol para protestar. ¿Para protestar por qué? La mujer mira al que le hace la pregunta de frente, esboza un gesto un poco indescifrable y responde: “Buff, por todo. Porque me encuentro en un callejón sin salida. Vivo con mis padres y con este sueldo ahora no puedo comprarme una casa nunca, ni siquiera alquilar yo sola. Por eso me puede la incertidumbre de no saber qué va a ser de mí. ¿Hasta cuándo voy a tener que estar en casa de mis padres? ¿Voy a tener que tener un hijo ahí? Tengo la sensación no de que he fracasado, porque no he fracasado, pero sí de que voy llegando tarde a todo.” A la siguiente pregunta: ¿vas a votar? Responde con un poco más de ánimo: “Pues obviamente. Hay que votar. Entiendo que la gente esté enfadada y frustrada con la política, pero hay que votar”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Maricarmen, mi vecina, símbolo a su pesar
items.description: El miércoles, ya de noche, poco después de que se anunciara su muerte , alguien colocó una rosa en el enrejado del portal del piso de Maricarmen en la calle de Sainz de Baranda. Una veintena de vecinos se reunió en silencio. Alguien colocó después la primera vela y escribió un pequeño texto de homenaje en una suerte de altar erigido en un alcorque que iría creciendo con las horas. La mujer acababa de morir en el hospital Gregorio Marañón, muy cerca de Sainz de Baranda. Tampoco muy lejos de allí, en Sol, en la acampada de más de 1.200 tiendas de campaña instaladas desde hacía 12 días, empezaba entonces a correr de boca en boca y de móvil en móvil la noticia del fallecimiento de la anciana. Álex, uno de los jóvenes acampados, recordaba así ese momento: “Y esta plaza, que siempre a esa hora, con asambleas y movidas, está llena de ruido, se calló de repente. Yo, que me había acercado al Corte Inglés para ir al servicio, al volver, sin saber aún nada, pensé que todo el mundo se había marchado de golpe, porque no se oía absolutamente nada”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La guerra entre ‘La revuelta’, ‘Cara al show’, ‘El hormiguero’, ‘El perro andaluz’… por dar con el invitado perfecto
items.description: Hace pocos años, si alguien promocionaba su película, libro, serie, teatro o, quizás simplemente, su persona, solo tenía un lugar en los canales generalistas al que dirigirse: El hormiguero . Todo cambió con el éxito de La revuelta de David Broncano en La 1 hace dos temporadas. Hoy un español puede recorrerse la televisión saltando entre formatos similares, mezcla de humor y entrevistas: puede empezar, por ejemplo, en Al cielo con ella y seguir en El perro andaluz , Cara al show o en las decenas de videopodcasts que llenan las redes sociales. En el centro del puzle, los coordinadores de invitados se han convertido en pieza clave del engranaje por su labor para gestionar la saturación de entrevistas a famosos. Su trabajo es, sin embargo, desconocido tras las cámaras. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Javier Urra: “Hay niños más viejos que yo: les hemos robado la esperanza”
items.description: Convoca en la sede de la Fundación Pequeño Deseo en Madrid, un piso sin lujos en un barrio de lujo, frente por frente del parque de El Retiro, en cuyas estancias se apretuja una pequeña multitud de empleadas y voluntarias, todas mujeres, afanándose con los teléfonos y los portátiles para cumplir las ilusiones de niños con enfermedades gravísimas. Urra , patrono de la Fundación, ha querido hablar aquí, porque la fundación acaba de presentar un estudio sobre los efectos benéficos, y duraderos, de esas iniciativas en 8.000 menores. Cuando llega de la sesión de fotos, mucho más delgado de lo que recordaba, lo primero que hace es obsequiarme con una cajita de bombones y tres de sus 91 libros publicados. En el bolsillo de la solapa de su chaqueta, la varita de hada coronada por una estrella dorada, emblema de la fundación. Lo tiene todo pensado. Seguir leyendo HURRA, URRA Javier Urra Portillo (Estella, Navarra, 69 años) irrumpió, entusiasta e hiperactivo, en la escena política, social y también mediática española cuando fue nombrado Defensor del Menor de la Comunidad de Madrid, el primero de España, por el entonces presidente madrileño. Alberto Ruiz Gallardón, en 1996. Aunque solo estuvo cinco años en el cargo, desde el que volvió a su plaza por oposición al Ministerio de Justicia como psicólogo de la Fiscalía de Menores, su nombre siguió, y sigue, asociado a la defensa de los derechos de los menores. Dedicado a la formación, la escritura y la gestión de varios centros privados de tratamiento a niños y adolescentes con problemas de comportamiento y salud mental, este doctor en Psicología y Ciencias de la Salud, y patrono de la Fundación Pequeño Deseo, acaba de anunciar que sufre un cáncer de mal pronóstico. Aunque ha reducido drásticamente su presencia pública en medios, sigue trabajando.

items.title: Un día de chicas para lobas y ‘minishakis’
items.description: “¿Te sabes el teléfono de mamá?”. La primera pregunta del guarda de seguridad no es muy rock and roll. Las parejas madre-niña somos mayoría a las 16.30 entre el público que empieza a llegar a la colorida entrada del Macondo Park que acoge la residencia musical de Shakira (13 conciertos, el último el día 12) en Madrid . “Estamos recomendando que se lo apunten en el brazo”, dice el segurata, pero la niña, que se llama Lupe, tiene 11 años y hoy lleva rímel, bate las pestañas en un gesto de autosuficiencia mientras recita el número. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La era de la crueldad
items.description: Hubo un tiempo, no tan lejano, en el que la burla del débil, la ofensa al enfermo o la humillación del desvalido quedaban excluidas del lenguaje democrático y el único espacio para estos discursos eran los rincones menos recomendables de la esfera política y mediática. No hace falta idealizar el pasado para recordar que a principios de este siglo un presidente de Estados Unidos del Partido Republicano como George W. Bush propugnaba un “conservadurismo compasivo” , porque consideraba que los valores de la derecha que él representaba no estaban en absoluto reñidos con la ayuda a los desfavorecidos o la escucha de los demás. Su sucesor, Barack Obama, defendía que el “déficit de empatía” era un problema más grave que el déficit presupuestario, y propugnaba el esfuerzo mental de “ponerse en los zapatos del otro” y “ver el mundo con sus ojos”. Todas estas buenas intenciones eran tal vez ingenuas, pero al menos mostraban una voluntad de decencia y ejemplaridad. Saltaron por los aires cuando Donald Trump irrumpió hace una década en la escena electoral llamando “violadores” a los inmigrantes mexicanos , gesticulando en un mitin para imitar a un periodista discapacitado o despreciando el historial bélico de alguien como John McCain, prisionero durante más de cinco años en Vietnam y considerado un héroe en su partido y su país. Ahí no había empatía ni compasión. Y solo era el principio. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Apocalipsis de andar por casa
items.description: Ignoro si el desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial acabará con la humanidad dentro de cuatro años, como pronostican los profetas del mal. Puede que no desaparezca físicamente del mapa, pero es probable que dentro de un corto plazo de tiempo, la humanidad mute en una especie distinta, más allá del carbono. Estamos todavía en la fase de las curiosidades que la IA nos proporciona, la alucinante rapidez a la hora de resolver el problema matemático más intrincado, el hecho de que pueda leer en un par de segundos todo lo que se ha escrito desde Sócrates. Primero fue la curiosidad, después el asombro, luego el vértigo, pero todo va a cambiar en cuanto tengamos conciencia de que la IA conoce los secretos más íntimos de nuestro cerebro y tiene la capacidad de condenarnos a ser sus esclavos. Entonces se instalará entre los humanos la culpa colectiva de haber deseado ser como dioses, según la promesa que hizo a Eva la serpiente al pie del árbol del paraíso. Se acerca el día en que las armas poseídas por la IA, carentes de ideología, lucharán entre ellas solo por el designio de destruirse por miedo a ser destruidas, como hasta ahora han hecho los humanos. ¿De quién recibirán las órdenes las armas inteligentes? ¿Quién mandará en las retaguardias? En las guerras la gente se mata por miedo a que la maten. Lo mismo sucederá en los arsenales. Cinco años fían los científicos para que este tipo de humanidad desparezca, en la que si vas al mercado las frutas serán todavía de verdad, los melones, los higos y los albaricoques; si un enamorado en la cama alarga la mano se encontrará con un cuerpo deseado de carne y hueso al que ama y reconoce por el tacto; si ves los telediarios comprobarás que los políticos idiotas de siempre no han mejorado y que nuestro destino está en manos de unos líderes mundiales que pugnan por parecerse al mono. Con suerte disponemos de un tiempo para degustar los placeres analógicos antes de convertirnos en esclavos.

items.title: Que nos hablen como adultos
items.description: Tal vez lo revolucionario, o lo que ahora nombran como punk, sea huir del exabrupto, del casticismo barato, de la burla, del escarnio, y presentarse a los demás como una persona bien educada, con esa educación sobria y cordial con la que definía Saul Bellow a los españoles en su viaje por España en los años cincuenta. Tal vez lo extraordinario hoy sea hablar y que suene a verdad, hablar para todos, escribir para todos, expresarse con el afán de ser entendido. Tal vez lo que deberían plantearse los políticos en el hoy más urgente es salir al estrado sin la pretensión de representar a un personaje, esforzarse en que lo que brille sea la inteligencia, no la ocurrencia. Pienso en el lenguaje. Tal vez lo que más debería plantearse la izquierda es cómo nos cuenta su programa, pero lo que escucho es un lenguaje plagado de lugares comunes que se nutre de las tertulias, la jerga académica o la publicidad. Puede que la razón sea que en España todos bebemos de la misma fuente, hasta el punto de que esos políticos que intervienen en las tertulias (me parece incompatible) acaben hablando como los contertulios y, a su vez, los contertulios, lo hacen como si en vez de remitirse a su análisis nos soltaran el mitin clerical de los domingos. Pone uno la radio de fondo y escucha expresiones en boga que muestran una uniformidad alarmante en el lenguaje público, discursos que denotan una gran pereza mental. Seguir leyendo

items.title: “No ayudes al enemigo”: Kiev alerta a Europa del peligro de la guerra híbrida rusa
items.description: El mensaje aparece sin subterfugios, de forma clara y contundente: “No ayudes al enemigo”. Así lo reclama y advierte a los ciudadanos a través de sus redes sociales Ukrzaliznytsia, la empresa nacional de ferrocarriles de Ucrania . Además de hacer frente a los bombardeos rusos, sufre otra vertiente de la guerra, la híbrida. Los responsables de los trenes tratan de abrir los ojos a aquellos que pueden caer en las redes del Kremlin a cambio de dinero u otros beneficios. Esta compañía, el principal empleador del país con más de 230.000 trabajadores, es uno de los objetivos más jugosos para los ataques de Moscú . De los trenes, responsables del transporte de personas y mercancías –incluido armamento– depende en buena medida la supervivencia y funcionamiento del país. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Las familias israelíes buscan descendencia en el esperma extraído de los cadáveres de sus hijos
items.description: La casa de Sharon Eizenkot sobrecoge. Todo gira en torno a Maor, su hijo muerto en 2023, cuando servía como soldado del ejército israelí en Gaza . Como si fuese un mausoleo del dolor, las paredes blancas no lucen más decoración que decenas de recuerdos, desde la camiseta de su equipo de fútbol hasta el uniforme y el rifle automático que llevaba cuando le alcanzó un artefacto explosivo en Jan Yunis. Él nunca lo sabrá, pero va a ser padre, previsiblemente en breve. Los militares que llamaron a la puerta de la madre para comunicarle el fallecimiento también le ofrecieron aprovechar la breve ventana de 72 horas para extraer tejido de los testículos del cadáver y obtener espermatozoides mientras fuesen útiles. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Una hora de tregua en Ceuta: la lavandería que iguala a policías y migrantes
items.description: En Ceuta hay lugares donde todos son doblemente extraños. Extraños entre sí y extraños en la ciudad. Este, en concreto, tiene una geometría casi burlona: apenas 20 metros dentro de los 20 kilómetros cuadrados de la ciudad autónoma, como un mundo pequeño dentro de otro mundo que se salió del eje con la entrada masiva de migrantes a finales de julio . Dos meses después, quedan pocas cosas que no hayan transformado su forma cotidiana; casi nada es como antes. Tampoco en esta lavandería de muros azules, donde todo finge ser igual de anónimo que siempre –solo gente entrando con ropa sucia y saliendo con ella limpia–, pero no lo es. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Un conflicto nuclear y el uso malicioso de la inteligencia artificial se cuelan entre las amenazas para la salud mundial: “Sería un apocalipsis”
items.description: Si para algo ha servido la pandemia de covid o la guerra en Ucrania es para constatar que situaciones inesperadas, completamente sobrevenidas e imprevisibles, pueden alterar drásticamente la salud y hasta poner en jaque a la humanidad. El peligro puede llegar en cualquier momento y desde cualquier parte, pero la comunidad científica ha identificado un puñado de amenazas con potencial especialmente dañino para la supervivencia humana. En un artículo publicado este domingo, una comisión de 37 expertos de la revista The Lancet señala 17 grandes riesgos para la salud mundial hasta 2100: a los sospechosos habituales, como las resistencias a los antibióticos, el cambio climático o la desnutrición, se han sumado otros desafíos emergentes, como el conflicto nuclear o el uso malicioso de la inteligencia artificial. “Aunque la probabilidad de ambos peligros sigue siendo baja, la magnitud del daño, si llegaran a materializarse, supondría un apocalipsis para la humanidad”, advierte la revista en un editorial adjunto. Seguir leyendo

items.description: “La banda era disciplinada, despiadada y muy organizada. Sus rufianes se pavoneaban por la ciudad como si les perteneciera. Y puede que así fuera: todo el mundo sabía quiénes eran y los policías corruptos no osaban arrestarlos.” Mark Galeotti (Surrey, Inglaterra, 60 años) arranca su nuevo libro, Homo criminalis. Cómo el crimen organiza el mundo (Capitán Swing), con una escena ficcionalizada de la cofradía de ladrones de Rinconete y Cortadillo de Cervantes que recuerda a El padrino o Peaky Blinders . items.title: ¿Vivienda, inmigración o Gobierno? Qué preocupa más a los votantes de cada partido
items.description: La vivienda es el principal problema de los españoles, pero está lejos de ser el único. Cada mes, el Centro de Investigaciones Sociológicas (CIS) pregunta a miles de personas: “¿Cuál es el principal problema que existe actualmente en España? ¿Y el segundo? ¿Y el tercero?”. La mayoría de los entrevistados mencionan, además del drama habitacional, a los políticos y a su forma de actuar, la inmigración o la crisis económica. Seguir leyendo Metodología Para los gráficos y las cifras de este artículo hemos analizado los microdatos de 75 barómetros del CIS, publicados entre diciembre de 2019 y septiembre de 2026. Hemos analizado las tres respuestas que da cada persona en los barómetros del CIS a la pregunta de cuáles son para él o ella los principales problemas. Para cada problema calculamos el porcentaje de entrevistados que lo menciona en cualquiera de esas posiciones. Si una persona lo repite, cuenta una sola vez: contamos personas que mencionan cada problema. Aplicamos después un ajuste de pesos llamado raking : damos algo más de peso a unas entrevistas y algo menos a otras para que, en conjunto, el recuerdo de voto y la participación reproduzcan los resultados de las elecciones generales de 2019 o 2023, según la fecha del barómetro. El ajuste incluye también la abstención y el voto blanco o nulo. No cambia lo que respondió nadie, sino cuánto contribuye cada respuesta al resultado. Para desglosar los problemas por votantes usamos, en cambio, su intención de voto actual, no el recuerdo empleado para calcular los pesos. Para mostrar la evolución de cada problema con menos ruido puntual, calculamos una media móvil. En los puntos interiores promediamos el barómetro anterior, el de ese mes y el siguiente. En el último punto, septiembre de 2026, la ventana se reduce a julio y septiembre Los gráficos 'treemaps' responden a otra pregunta: cómo se reparte por intención de voto el conjunto de personas que menciona cada problema. Para ellos mantenemos la media de junio, julio y septiembre de 2026, dando el mismo peso a cada barómetro. Por eso su ventana de cálculo no coincide exactamente con la del último punto del gráfico de evolución.

items.title: Cómo movilizar a un votante bombardeado y enfadado
items.description: Una campaña electoral es, fundamentalmente, un contexto. O varios, actuando simultáneamente y entrecruzados. La que comienza en España y acabará el próximo 29-N no es ajena a un escenario internacional complejo y, a priori, adverso para el actual presidente. Por supuesto que hay temas nacionales, pero hoy las campañas son globales y están interconectadas como nunca. Incluyendo injerencias, explícitas y subterráneas; con tecnologías y algoritmos omnipresentes; y una industria electoral también mercenaria. Vivimos corrientes políticas y sociales que trascienden fronteras. Y los ciclos electorales existen. Las elecciones pueden ser generales, pero ya no son solo nacionales. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Juan Carlos Ferrero: “Ojalá hubiera disfrutado más, he sido demasiado cuadriculado”
items.description: Juan Carlos Ferrero (Ontinyent, Valencia; 46 años) llega a la cita con EL PAÍS conduciendo directamente desde Villena (Alicante). El encuentro tiene lugar en un hotel cercano a Atocha y cuenta con banda sonora, la del chaparrón de sobremesa que golpea con fuerza la cubierta de metacrilato. El técnico, en su día sensación de 20 años, se recuesta sobre el sofá, sorbe café y se explaya: toda una carrera, toda una vida. Y ahora una inmersión introspectiva, el libro Mentalidad ganadora (Impulsa). Repasa durante una hora el viaje que le llevó del pueblo a la explosión del Sant Jordi , y de ahí al vertiginoso vuelo con Carlos Alcaraz. Ahora quiere volver al circuito, pero asegura que todavía no ha escogido el proyecto. “No tengo hecho nada con nadie”. Se despide y matiza: “Nos vemos pronto”. “O tal vez no… Ya veremos lo que pasa”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El cantante Jaime Anglada se prepara para su regreso a los escenarios: “Siento como si el accidente hubiera acelerado mi vejez”
items.description: “La verdad es que me encuentro bien, afortunado sabiendo todo lo que me ha pasado”. El cantante Jaime Anglada (Palma, 54 años) se siente una persona diferente después del accidente que sufrió en agosto de 2025 y que casi le cuesta la vida. Aquella madrugada de verano regresaba a casa en su moto, después de ver un concierto del músico Nando González en un conocido local de Palma, cuando fue embestido por un vehículo conducido por un joven que se dio a la fuga y que triplicaba la tasa permitida de alcohol en sangre. Anglada pasó varios días en coma inducido en el hospital de Son Espases de Mallorca y, tras despertar, comenzó un largo proceso de recuperación que sigue a día de hoy, y que le ha mantenido lejos de los escenarios durante 14 meses. “Todavía noto que estoy en un proceso, no sé hasta cuándo durará. Encuentro que ahora soy una persona más lenta y siento como si el accidente hubiera acelerado mi vejez”, explica en una entrevista con EL PAÍS. Seguir leyendo

items.title: The lost civilian CT body
items.description: THIS is an obituary for the National Counter Terrorism Authority, once conceived as a civilian counterterrorism body that combined policymaking, coordination among law-enforcement agencies, and data collection and processing. Since its inception in December 2008, and even after gaining legal cover under the Nacta Act, 2013, it has struggled to fully realise its role and mandate, while facing resistance from LEAs reluctant to coordinate with a police-led body. Appointing a senior military officer as its national coordinator was not the first deviation from the Nacta Act. A bigger departure from the statute had come in 2025 with the establishment of the National Intelligence Fusion and Threat Assessment Centre. Niftac was created as a parallel body, apparently under Nacta but in effect superior to it, even though Nacta is the statutory body. This gave a superior security institution the leading role. Nacta’s new form seems to have little to do with developing a counterterrorism strategy, building a coordination mechanism, or taking on a CT-related operational role. Its real purpose is to synchronise all civilian-led LEAs with the superior security institution, and, at the very least, to bring them under one roof. This synchronisation of internal security policy with the security doctrine conceived by the establishment’s top brass has been underway for a long time, taking various forms. Bureaucrats see it in the National Security and War Course (NSWC) at the National Defence University (NDU), which is now equivalent to the National Management Course, a mandatory course for promotion from Grade 20 to 21. The NSWC gives senior bureaucrats more opportunities to align with evolving thinking at the top levels of the security institutions. At the narrative level, NDU and many other military-led institutions run short courses for opinion-makers, politicians, and business and community leaders to align them with the new thought process. Interestingly, all these courses and discourses happen at the expense of civilian governments, whether provincial or federal. Nacta, the only civilian-led CT body, struggled to find its role and eventually lost. One may argue that synchronisation within the internal security structure will improve coordination, the very dream for which Nacta was conceived. However, the new changes appear to be aimed at control, and the CT body is being used as an instrument of that. The structures of other LEAs, such as the police and FIA, leave little room for intervention by other institutions — unlike Nacta. Admittedly, Nacta had a few good leaders who clearly understood the terrorism challenge facing the country and how to respond. But it is safe to say that most of its heads, and even others who served in the authority, had little idea of the CT body’s objectives. Many came on deputation, or to rest before landing a field posting. As mentioned earlier, Nacta faced pressure and challenges from superior security institutions, which were reluctant to work under or with a civilian-led body. Still, the police cadre is undoubtedly responsible for destroying the institution and providing an excuse for its takeover. This did not happen overnight. The process began much earlier. When former prime minister Imran Khan chaired the Nacta board of governors meeting in September 2018, as required by law, two key realities emerged. One, he was the first prime minister to convene a board meeting since the Act was passed, even though quarterly meetings were required. Two, the national coordinator at the time recommended that the prime minister dissolve the body, as it had no use or role in countering terrorism in the country. This was the first and last board meeting held under the original Act. In July 2019, parliament amended it through an ordinance, which it later passed in March 2020. The amendment made the interior minister the board chairman and the national coordinator its secretary. Several references to the “prime minister” in the Act were also replaced, shifting Nacta’s reporting line to the interior ministry. The 2019-2020 amendments thus downgraded Nacta from a prime minister-led federal-provincial body to one under the interior minister. Interestingly, one of the few board meetings held since then, and chaired by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, approved the establishment of Niftac. Just before Niftac was introduced, Nacta inducted around 130 permanent officers. Since Niftac’s establishment, most have struggled to find a role. Niftac was described as a national platform connecting more than 50 federal and provincial departments and agencies — supported by provincial fusion centres — to improve intelligence coordination, speed up threat assessment, and strengthen information-sharing across institutional boundaries. That was Nacta’s purpose. A military or intelligence institution can possess information that a civilian authority cannot access. It can conduct operations a civilian institution cannot. It can assess threats from a classified perspective. But the state also needs an institution that can sit openly with provincial police, civil administration, prosecutors, courts, parliamentarians, researchers and international partners. It needs an institution whose authority is intelligible within the civilian legal and administrative system. Against this backdrop, Niftac overshadowed Nacta. Even before Maj Gen Faisal Naseer was appointed national coordinator, Niftac and its officers from the superior security institutions appeared more assertive and powerful than the national coordinator. In fact, Nacta, the only civilian-led CT body, struggled to find its role and eventually lost that struggle. Now the vision and implementation plan will flow top-down, and space for consultation, policy discourse, and debate will gradually vanish. This institutional transformation is taking place at a time when Pakistan faces its worst terrorism challenge, one that is growing more complex by the day. The state is trying hard to find a way out of the menace, but these transformations will not solve it. Concentrating power in one set of hands can be challenging because absolute control centralises the burden. The writer is a security analyst. Published in Dawn, October 11th, 2026

items.title: Sri Lankan vet returns home amid concerns over Madhubala’s health
items.description: KARACHI: Sri Lankan wildlife health specialist Dr Buddhika Bandara, who had joined efforts to save Madhubala on Friday, left for home the same day under unclear circumstances, raising concern over Safari Park’s administrative affairs as well as the ongoing health crisis confronting the ailing elephant, it emerged on Saturday. Sources told Dawn that local authorities had not informed the visiting Sri Lankan expert that he would be working with Dr Amir Khalil of the global animal welfare organisation Four Paws at Safari Park. “It seems this situation damaged the trust between the two parties, forcing him to leave quietly. Madhubala’s deteriorating condition must have shocked him, too,” shared an official, adding that Dr Bandara’s hesitation to speak at Friday’s presser surprised many journalists who had requested him several times to share his clinical observations of Madhubala. The sources also expressed concern over the fact that the Safari Park authorities kept Four Paws out for over a year — a critical time during which Madhubala received TB treatment and later developed multiple infections and acute weakness —and then sought its help just three weeks ago when Madhubala’s condition worsened. KMC spokesperson says Dr Bandara left due to death of a family member in Colombo Responding to these concerns, Karachi Metropolitan Corporation’s spokesperson Daniyal Siyal said that Dr Bandara had been monitoring Madhubala’s TB treatment online since his first visit over a year ago. “He had to leave due to the sudden death of his family member in Colombo. Even last month, he was in touch with us. Last year, he stayed with us for 17 days [for Madhubala’s treatment] and this time, his stay was planned for at least a week,” he explained. All support was being extended to Dr Khalil, he added. The foreign experts were invited by local authorities after Safari Park vets had failed to diagnose the factors behind Madhubala’s ongoing health crisis. The female African elephant has experienced drastic weight loss in recent months and collapsed twice in her enclosure. According to Dr Khalil, multiple bacterial and parasitic infections and the weakness that followed treatment for tuberculosis have caused Madhubala to lose significant weight. Additionally, she seems to suffer from a linear fracture in the carpal joint. Published in Dawn, October 11th, 2026
