items.title: La Diaspora : Un pont culturel entre l’Allemagne et le Sénégal
items.description: Estimée à environ 6 500 personnes, la diaspora sénégalaise en Allemagne se distingue par son intégration exemplaire au sein de la société allemande. Elle entend désormais jouer un rôle plus actif pour le renforcement des investissements. Selon les données officielles du service de l’immigration, environ 6 500 ressortissants sénégalais sont recensés en Allemagne, un chiffre qui ne reflète toutefois pas l’intégralité des bi-nationaux ni l’ensemble de la communauté résidente. « La majeure partie de notre communauté est établie au sein des grands centres urbains et des bassins économiques comme Berlin, la région Rhin-Ruhr, Francfort, Munich ou Hambourg », explique Mme Raky Touré Winkelhog, présidente et fondatrice des « Sénégalais d’Allemagne » et membre de « Sénégal Sama Rew ». D’après elle, la communauté sénégalaise en Allemagne se distingue par sa discrétion et son intégration exemplaire au sein de la société allemande, portées par un engagement associatif soutenu, la maîtrise de la langue et une contribution active à la vie citoyenne et économique. « Nos membres évoluent aujourd’hui dans des secteurs très diversifiés, allant de l’éducation et la santé jusqu’à l’ingénierie et l’entrepreneuriat », indique Mme Winkelhog. L’homme politique Karamba Diaby est l’un des représentants éminents de la diaspora sénégalaise en Allemagne. Né au Sénégal, il a rejoint l’Allemagne pour ses études : il est notamment titulaire d’un doctorat en géoécologie soutenue en 1996 à l’Université Martin-Luther de Halle-Wittenberg. En 2013, il est devenu la première personne noire née en Afrique à être élue au Bundestag allemand pour la circonscription de Halle/Saale. « Mon histoire montre que les relations entre l’Allemagne et le Sénégal peuvent produire quelque chose de particulièrement précieux : des parcours de vie qui relient les deux pays et créent des ponts humains, scientifiques, économiques et culturels », explique-t-il. Il a visiblement fait des émules puisqu’un autre ressortissant sénégalais, M. Saliou Gueye, a été élu maire de Stuttgart-Zuffenhausen, un arrondissement d’environ 40 000 habitants. « Mon parcours m’a permis de comprendre que les relations entre l’Allemagne et le Sénégal ne doivent pas être considérées uniquement comme des relations entre deux gouvernements. Elles vivent aussi dans les villes, les quartiers, les universités, les associations, les entreprises et, surtout, à travers les femmes et les hommes qui créent des ponts entre les deux sociétés », déclare M. Gueye. Tout comme Karamba Diaby, Saliou Gueye croit profondément que la diaspora peut être une véritable force citoyenne, professionnelle, économique et politique. « Elle dispose de compétences, d’expériences, de réseaux et d’une capacité d’engagement qui peuvent contribuer pleinement au développement, à la fois de son pays d’accueil et de son pays d’origine ». Raky Touré Winkelhog évoque l’image d’un arbre pour décrire le rôle de la diaspora : les racines sont ancrées au Sénégal, le tronc en Allemagne et les feuilles incarnent le métissage des deux sociétés. « Cette double culture nous permet d’aborder l’avenir des relations germano-sénégalaises avec une ambition renouvelée », souligne Raky Touré Winkelhog. Pour Saliou Gueye, les collectivités territoriales peuvent également jouer un rôle beaucoup plus important. Il cite l’exemple de la coopération entre Ludwigsburg et Kongoussi (Burkina Faso) qui montre que les partenariats entre villes peuvent produire des résultats très concrets. Dans le cadre de la coopération germano-sénégalais, il souhaiterait donc voir davantage de partenariats directs entre villes, universités, entreprises, associations et acteurs de la diaspora. Celle-ci constitue à ses yeux « un pont stratégique entre les deux pays », puisqu’elle connaît les deux sociétés, parle les deux langues, comprend les deux cultures et dispose d’une expérience précieuse. Au total, Karamba Diaby se dit fondamentalement optimiste quant à l’avenir des relations entre l’Allemagne et le Sénégal. Toutefois, il plaide pour un changement de paradigme. « La coopération de demain doit être davantage fondée sur le partenariat, la réciprocité et la co-construction », explique l’ancien député au Parlement fédéral allemand, citant quatre moteurs essentiels : la jeunesse, la connaissance, l’économie et la société civile. Dans cette perspective, la diaspora entend être un vecteur de sécurisation et d’orientation des investissements, conclut Raky Touré Winkelhog. Par Seydou KA

items.title: BRICS Or Balance? What Ghana’s bid really means
items.description: Ghana’s decision to apply to join BRICS is not a diplomatic footnote; it is a strategic signal. On October 6, 2026, Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa announced that Cabinet had decided to pursue membership, saying the objective was to diversify partnerships, widen economic opportunities and deepen cooperation with the Global South. .India, whose foreign minister was visiting Accra, has been approached to help Ghana navigate the application. The World Bank puts Ghana’s 2025 GDP at $114.2 billion, with 6.0 percent growth, while its population stands at 35.1 million. Ghana is not a great power seeking to rewrite the international system or dictate the rules of global commerce. It is a middle-sized African state seeking more room to manoeuvre within it. BRICS has grown considerably beyond the original Brazil-Russia-India-China grouping. Its current membership comprises 11 states, representing about 49 percent of the world’s population, 39 percent of global GDP and 23 percent of international trade. Its expanding economic and geopolitical weight offers Accra a platform for trade, investment and diplomatic coalition-building. Membership could provide another channel for engaging major emerging economies, reducing excessive dependence on traditional Western partners and broadening Ghana’s strategic options. The attraction is not ideological alignment with every member, but the opportunity to operate in a wider economic and diplomatic ecosystem as global power becomes more dispersed. Membership, however, is not automatic. Ghana has announced a bid, not secured a seat. BRICS says accession moves from formal interest to potential membership and then full membership, with Sherpas, foreign ministers and ultimately leaders deciding by consensus. Accra must demonstrate that its application can win political support from members. The bid is therefore the opening move in a consequential geopolitical negotiation, not a guaranteed victory. The test is whether Ghana can convert its interest into gains without damaging longstanding relationships with the United States, European Union and other Western partners. The Economic Logic Is Powerful, But Not Magical Ghana already trades heavily with BRICS economies, China and India. Ghana-China trade reached a record $14.1 billion in 2025, up 19.3 percent. In 2024, China supplied 45.9 percent of Ghana’s imports from Asia, while India supplied 13.7 percent. This concentration creates opportunity and vulnerability. A formal BRICS relationship could help Ghana move beyond buying manufactured goods and exporting raw commodities, supporting investment in processing, infrastructure, digital technology, energy and transport. The New Development Bank makes the prospect relevant. It has $52.7 billion in paid-in capital and supports development projects across member countries. For a country seeking infrastructure and industrial financing, engagement with the BRICS ecosystem could open additional channels of capital and development cooperation. But BRICS cannot substitute for economic reform. Ghana’s debt problems, currency risks, productivity constraints and dependence on commodities will not disappear because Accra sits at the table. Diplomatic access is not guaranteed investment, and every proposed project must still meet Ghana’s needs, affordability tests and transparency standards. The strategic prize is bargaining power. Ghana could use closer ties with China, India, Brazil, the Gulf and other emerging economies to negotiate from a broader base with Western partners. The objective should not be to replace one sphere of dependence with another, but to expand Ghana’s room for manoeuvre. Membership can strengthen that position if Accra treats it as an instrument of diversification and strategic autonomy. The Security Question Is More Complicated BRICS is not a military alliance and offers no Article 5-style collective-defence commitment. Its significance is political: it provides a forum for coordinating positions on global governance, sanctions, development and the international order. Joining would not give Ghana a BRICS security guarantee against jihadist violence spilling south from the Sahel, maritime insecurity in the Gulf of Guinea or cyber threats. Ghana’s existing Western security relationships remain substantial. In August 2026, the Defence Ministry said US cooperation included joint exercises, intelligence sharing, counter-terrorism support, maritime security and plans involving drone-based intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance. In September, Ghana reaffirmed its defence and security partnership with Washington, including logistics, institutional development, peacekeeping, cyber defence and maritime security. Strategic balance is essential. Accra should not allow BRICS membership to undermine interoperability with the United States, European partners or African security institutions. The objective should be diversification rather than substitution: add partnerships, markets and diplomatic options without trading one dependency for another. The Geopolitical Price of Greater Autonomy The deeper consequence is diplomatic. Ghana’s bid would place it more visibly in the debate over whether the international system should remain predominantly Western-led or become more plural and representative. BRICS says it seeks stronger Global South participation and reform of global governance. A stronger voice within Global South coalitions could reinforce its calls to reform institutions whose voting structures often lag behind economic realities. But autonomy has a cost. BRICS includes China and Russia, whose relations with the United States and its allies are marked by strategic rivalry and, in Russia’s case, war-related sanctions. Ghana may face pressure to clarify positions on sanctions, conflicts, technology standards and contested international norms. BRICS criteria emphasize good relations among members, support for governance reform and, for partners, avoiding unilateral sanctions not authorized by the UN Security Council. Accra must be disciplined. Ghana should join only if it can preserve what has made its foreign policy effective: flexibility, credibility and the ability to work across competing blocs. The objective is strategic autonomy, not bloc politics. The smartest policy is conditional engagement. Ghana should seek market access, investment, technology, development finance and diplomatic leverage from BRICS while maintaining US and European security partnerships, ECOWAS commitments and wider African obligations. The test is simple: does membership expand Ghana’s choices? If yes, the bid is strategically sound. If it merely replaces one external dependence with another, it is not diversification; it is dependency under a different flag. Ghana’s geopolitical asset is not allegiance, but room to manoeuvre as rival powers compete for influence. Ghana is not choosing between East and West. It is trying to ensure that, in an increasingly fractured world, it has enough partners to choose for itself. — The writer is a lecturer in journalism and media studies and the CEO of The International Lens (theinternationallens.com).

items.title: Adamus Resources launches breast cancer awareness campaign in Nzema
items.description: Adamus Resources Limited has launched a breast cancer awareness campaign in Nzema in the Western Region as part of activities marking Breast Cancer Awareness Month. The campaign, spearheaded by the Adamus Ladies Association, seeks to promote early detection, encourage regular breast examinations and educate women on the importance of seeking prompt medical attention. The launch, held at the company’s mining premises in the Ellembelle District, brought together female employees, health professionals and other participants under the theme, “Every Story Is Unique, Every Journey Matters.” Addressing participants, gynaecologist Dr Roland Paaga stressed the importance of early diagnosis in improving breast cancer treatment outcomes. He cautioned against delays in seeking medical attention after detecting unusual changes in the breast, explaining that late diagnosis could complicate treatment. Dr Paaga also drew attention to the fact that breast cancer affects both women and men, although the disease is more common among women. He encouraged regular breast health checks and urged participants to seek professional medical advice whenever they notice unusual symptoms. The Corporate Affairs and Public Relations Officer of Adamus Resources Limited, Archangel Kaku Bennett, said the campaign formed part of the company’s commitment to improving healthcare awareness and supporting the wellbeing of people in its operational communities. He explained that the company, through the Adamus Ladies Association, had undertaken several health education initiatives focusing on women’s health, menstrual hygiene and reproductive health. Mr Bennett announced plans to extend the breast cancer awareness campaign to Kwame Nkrumah Senior High School at Nsein in the Nzema East Municipality and the Asanta community in the Ellembelle District. The outreach programmes will provide breast health education and screening opportunities for women and young girls. The President of the Adamus Ladies Association, Hannah Chemel, urged women to overcome the fear and stigma associated with breast cancer and seek medical attention when they notice unusual changes in their breasts. She discouraged self-medication and delays in seeking treatment, stressing that early diagnosis could significantly improve treatment outcomes. Some participants welcomed the initiative and appealed for similar programmes to be extended to more communities across Nzema. The campaign forms part of activities marking Breast Cancer Awareness Month, observed globally every October to promote awareness, early detection and access to treatment.

items.title: Quand la banane algérienne s’invite au royaume des agrumes à Blida
items.description: La banane va-t-elle s’imposer dans le fief même des agrumes en Algérie ? Alors que le prix de ce fruit exotique atteint des pics historiques et se fait de plus en plus rare sur les étals des commerces, il est en abondance dans cette exploitation agricole située à Mouzaia dans la wilaya de Blida. Dans cette région réputée pour ses agrumes, la banane tente de se faire place. L’exploitation a reçu la visite des responsables de la Chambre d’agriculture de Blida qui ont été séduits par cet investissement. De la banane produite au royaume des agrumes à Blida « La visite d’aujourd’hui ne s’est pas déroulée ni en Équateur ni aux Philippines. Elle a lieu dans la commune de Mouzaïa, chez Ahmed Baraka à l’exploitation Halifi Ali n° 06, où la banane est produite selon des normes internationales », s’est félicitée la Chambre d’agriculture de Blida à l’issue de la visite. Lors de cette visite, la Chambre était représentée par son président, Brahim Belhadef, son secrétaire général, Mohamed Hand et un membre du conseil d’administration, Djebbar Rachid. Le président de l’association de développement rural, Benaouda Mohamed, était également présent. L’exploitation a reçu la visite des responsables de la Chambre d’agriculture de Blida De la banane produite à Blida, mais à quel prix ? « Cette exploitation de culture de bananes est conforme aux standards internationaux, dans une wilaya connue pour la production d’agrumes », a ajouté la Chambre d’agriculture de Blida qui a salué cette « expérience unique en son genre, une réussite remarquable tant sur le plan de la quantité que de la qualité ». Toutefois, aucune indication chiffrée n’a été fournie sur cette exploitation. Les surfaces plantées et les quantités produites n’ont pas été précisées. Le problème lié à la consommation d’eau que demande les bananiers n’a pas été abordé alors qu’il constitue un élément clé dans tout investissement agricole. L’article Quand la banane algérienne s’invite au royaume des agrumes à Blida est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Police foil plot to kidnap Abuja prophetess, arrest 4 suspects
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Intelligence Response Team (IRT) of the Nigeria Police Force has foiled an alleged plot to kidnap a prophetess and assistant Pastor in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, and arrested four suspects with a locally fabricated firearm and a vehicle allegedly acquired for the operation. Parading the suspects as part of recent operations targeting kidnapping, armed robbery and other violent crimes in the nation’s Federal Capital Territory, Commander of IRT, DCP Adamu Muazu noted that the alleged plot was particularly disturbing because some of the suspects were members of the same church with the intended victim, identified as Prophetess Elizabeth. Muazu said the Prophetess Elizabeth had reportedly given testimony in church about her personal achievements and business success, after which some members of the congregation allegedly began planning her abduction. He disclosed that one of the suspects, David Obaje, was said to have worked as Elizabeth’s driver for about three months and had been a member of the church for approximately four years, giving him knowledge of her movements and routines. DCP Muazu added that another suspect, David Dennis, reportedly belonged to the church for about six years and worked as a bodyguard to the senior pastor. The Commander said Police investigators alleged that the suspects used a WhatsApp group to coordinate the planned kidnapping and had also arranged for another person to be brought from Kogi State to participate in the operation. He added that the suspects planned to attack Elizabeth after an evening church service on October 1 by using a vehicle to block or deliberately hit her car, creating the appearance of a road accident and forcing her to stop. “She would then allegedly be overpowered and taken to a predetermined location where she was expected to be held”. The IRT boss further explained that the investigation led to the recovery of the vehicle allegedly acquired for the operation, as well as a firearm reportedly procured for the planned abduction. Revealing that the suspects claimed the weapon was purchased from a vigilante group for N120,000, the IRT Commander described the recovered weapon as a locally fabricated AK-47. He said Investigators also recovered a security uniform allegedly obtained as part of preparations for the operation. The Commander, however, disclosed that the planned abduction was disrupted after the IRT received intelligence about the alleged conspiracy and arrested the suspects before the operation could be carried out. DCP Muazu warned members of the public against disclosing sensitive personal information, particularly details about their finances, businesses, properties, movements and personal achievements in public gatherings. He urged churches to strengthen security around their premises, especially during evening services, through adequate lighting, controlled access and proper monitoring of people and vehicles. DCP Muazu assured Nigerians that the IRT would continue to deploy intelligence-led operations to disrupt criminal networks and prevent planned attacks. The post Police foil plot to kidnap Abuja prophetess, arrest 4 suspects appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: GPRTU wants full TRAFFITECH-GH implementation to start in 2027
items.description: The Ghana Private Road Transport Union has asked the police to postpone the full implementation of TRAFFITECH-GH to 2027, citing concerns over inadequate preparation and public education ahead of the November 1 rollout. The union’s Deputy Public Relations Officer, Samuel Amoah, said the necessary infrastructure and enforcement equipment must be ready before the system is implemented. Speaking in a television interview with Channel One News on Friday, [October 9], he acknowledged the system’s potential to improve road discipline but questioned whether the authorities were adequately prepared. “It is very good they are bringing it just to make sure that there will be sanity on our roads. Drivers will comply. Police will also not be disturbing drivers or taking money from drivers but the question is, the infrastructure they have to put in place, are they ready?” he questioned. Mr Amoah said some police officers he had spoken to did not fully understand how the system would operate. “Trust me, I once spoke to some police personnel. They don’t even understand the whole thing,” he said. He urged the authorities to use the remaining time to educate motorists and ensure officers were adequately prepared before enforcement begins. “If the authorities can even push it to the end of the year so that we can start from next year, so that effective education and sensitisation will be done,” he added. Mr Amoah also called for the necessary devices to be made available to help police officers check drivers’ licences and other documents. He cautioned against focusing primarily on revenue from traffic offences, saying the system should prioritise road safety and compliance.

items.title: How 10-mile walks for basic education birthed a 50-year legal career for Justice Korbieh
items.description: Long before he donned the judicial robes of the Court of Appeal or occupied a seat in Parliament, retired Justice Francis Gyafiiry Korbieh was simply a young boy in the Upper West Region, trekking 10 miles on foot just to acquire a basic primary education. That gruelling weekly pilgrimage through the rugged terrain of Jirapa laid the groundwork for a legendary 50-year career in Ghana’s legal profession, proving that no distance is too far for a mind determined to learn. Speaking on Joy FM’s Personality Profile , the veteran jurist recounted how the utter lack of educational infrastructure in his native village forced him into an arduous routine from an early age. “Well, let me start by saying that I come from a village that is 10 miles due east of Jirapa,” Justice Korbieh recalled. “There was no school there. So I had to walk those 10 miles, let me say 10 kilometres.” A grueling weekly trek for knowledge With no primary school in his immediate community, the young Korbieh had to rely on a weekly boarding arrangement at his school in Jirapa. However, the trek to and from campus remained a punishing ritual that tested his resolve throughout his six years of primary education. “I used to walk to the school, attend school for one week, walk back to my village for two days and then walk back to school for another week,” he revealed. That relentless sacrifice paid off in Primary Six when his academic promise earned him a spot among the pioneer students at the newly established St. Francis Xavier Minor Seminary—a rare feat for a child from the region to transition directly into secondary school at the time. “It was a novelty at the time because in our part of the country, nobody ever went to secondary school from Primary Six,” he noted. From humble footsteps to the bench Though the seminary aimed to train young men for the Catholic priesthood, Korbieh ultimately chose a different calling. “I didn’t want to become a priest,” he said with a laugh. “I didn’t get the calling. So that’s why I didn’t become a priest. But here I am. I serve my country very well. I also serve the church very well.” That service blossomed into a distinguished career. Born on 20 December 1950 at Jirapa/Kuncheni, Justice Korbieh pursued further studies at St. Peter’s Secondary School, the University of Ghana, and the Ghana School of Law. He was called to the Ghana Bar on 30 September 1976, marking five decades in the legal fraternity this year. He went on to serve as the Member of Parliament for Jirapa from 1993 to 2001 before elevating to the Bench, where he served as a Justice of the Court of Appeal until his retirement in 2020. Yet, for the retired judge, the foundation of every judgment written and every law passed remains those 10 long miles walked in pursuit of a dream.

items.title: Des écoles de Saint-Louis toujours dans les eaux
items.description: À deux jours de la rentrée scolaire prévue le lundi 12 octobre, la situation reste préoccupante dans certains établissements scolaires de Saint-Louis, notamment aux quartiers Médina Course et Pikine où les eaux de pluie compliquent les préparatifs. Par contre, les écoles de la ville et du faubourg de Sor affichent un visage plus rassurant. SAINT-LOUIS- À Saint-Louis, on peut sans se tromper dire que la rentrée est suspendue à la météo dans certains établissements scolaires. À l’approche de cet événement prévu le lundi 12 octobre, l’hivernage continue de peser sur les préparatifs. Dans les quartiers les plus exposés aux inondations, les équipes s’activent à rendre les établissements accessibles afin de permettre aux élèves de retrouver les salles de classe dans des conditions acceptables. Mais entre les eaux stagnantes dans les cours, les accès difficiles et les infrastructures affectées, le compte à rebours est particulièrement serré. Au Collège d’enseignement moyen (Cem) de Médina Course le constat est préoccupant. C’est aussi le cas à l’école élémentaire Boubacar Diop où une importante quantité d’eau occupe une partie de la cour. Dans cet établissement, l’accès aux salles de classe reste compliqué. Les traces de l’hivernage sont visibles, témoignant des difficultés auxquelles l’équipe pédagogique doit faire face à quelques jours de la reprise des enseignements. Sur place les sapeurs-pompiers sont mobilisés. Le dispositif de pompage déployé doit permettre d’évacuer les eaux et de libérer progressivement les espaces envahis. Une course contre la montre est engagée pour rendre l’établissement praticable avant l’arrivée des élèves. Le directeur de l’école Mbaye Niang ne cache pas ses inquiétudes. « On ne peut pas dire que tout est parfait pour le moment. Il y a de l’eau stagnante au niveau de la cour, mais également dans certaines salles de classe. L’accès aussi est un peu difficile », a-t-il expliqué, évoquant les conséquences des fortes précipitations enregistrées ces derniers jours. Face à cette situation, la direction de l’établissement indique travailler en coordination avec les autorités académiques et les services compétents pour accélérer le retour à la normale. Les sapeurs-pompiers et les services d’hygiène sont notamment sollicités pour contribuer à l’évacuation des eaux et à l’assainissement des lieux. Malgré ces difficultés, le personnel enseignant est déjà présent. Les équipes administratives poursuivent également leurs activités, même si l’accueil des élèves demeure, pour elles, une préoccupation majeure. « Les enseignants ont fait leur entrée normalement. Ils sont pratiquement tous là. Mais pour recevoir les élèves, c’est un peu compliqué », a souligné Mbaye Niang. Les abris provisoires bien impactés Le responsable espère toutefois une amélioration rapide de la situation. L’objectif, dit-il, est de permettre aux enseignements de démarrer dès lundi, à condition que les opérations de pompage aboutissent et que de nouvelles précipitations ne viennent pas aggraver les difficultés. Juste à côté se trouve le Cem de Médina Course. Ici, le spectacle est saisissant. Une large nappe d’eau trouble recouvre une partie de la cour. À la surface, des débris et des matériaux de chantier témoignent des difficultés auxquelles l’établissement est confronté. Les abords des bâtiments sont encore humides et certains accès restent difficiles à emprunter. Dans cette école, nous n’avons pas trouvé de personnel administratif et enseignant sur place, mais les sapeurs-pompiers sont à pied d’œuvre. Un système de pompage est déployé pour évacuer les eaux et tenter de rendre les lieux praticables avant l’arrivée des élèves. L’opération se poursuit alors que le calendrier scolaire impose une intervention rapide. À ces problèmes d’inondation s’ajoute la dégradation des abris provisoires de l’établissement. L’état de ces structures constitue un autre sujet de préoccupation. Selon le directeur de l’école Boubacar Diop, les difficultés d’accès compliquent la mobilité des parents d’élèves. L’espoir est de voir la situation évoluer dans les prochains jours afin que les familles puissent accomplir les formalités nécessaires en cette veille de rentrée. À Pikine, le constat n’est guère plus rassurant. L’école élémentaire, dont le portail était fermé lors de notre passage, présente des murs marqués par l’humidité et des abords encombrés de déchets et de matériaux divers. À proximité, le lycée de Pikine offre aussi une image préoccupante. Une partie de la cour est occupée par des eaux stagnantes. Des ouvriers sont visibles dans l’enceinte laissant apparaître un environnement où des travaux semblent encore en cours. Ici, la situation exige également une vigilance particulière. Dans ce secteur vulnérable de la banlieue saint-louisienne, les pluies et les inondations risquent de compromettre la rentrée même si le proviseur du lycée, Alioune Badara Diallo assure que des efforts ont été consentis pour évacuer les eaux et nettoyer les salles de classe. Une équipe chargée du cadre de vie est notamment intervenue pour renforcer les opérations de nettoyage. « Les eaux de pluie qui étaient en stagnation au niveau du lycée ont été évacuées. Il reste quelques flaques, mais les salles de classe sont déjà très propres », a-t-il affirmé. Pour le proviseur, l’enjeu est désormais de réunir les conditions pouvant permettre aux élèves de reprendre le chemin de l’école. Mais cette perspective reste étroitement liée à l’évolution de la météo. Dans cette zone régulièrement confrontée aux inondations, une nouvelle pluie importante pourrait compromettre les efforts engagés. « Quand il pleut à Pikine, le lycée n’est pas praticable », prévient Alioune Badara Diallo qui espère une accalmie pour assurer un démarrage normal des cours. Le décor est toutefois différent dans plusieurs établissements de la ville et du faubourg de Sor. Dans ces zones, aucune difficulté majeure liée aux inondations n’a été signalée. Les établissements visités présentent des conditions plus favorables à la rentrée. Tout le contraire à Médina Course et à Pikine. Jeanne SAGNA (Correspondante)

items.title: Mahama announces plans to import electric wheelchairs for PWDs
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has announced plans by the government to import rechargeable electric wheelchairs for persons with disabilities (PWDs). He explained that the pilot project was intended to facilitate the mobility of PWDs and said the wheelchairs would be handed over to the National Council on Persons with Disability upon arrival. The President made the announcement during a citizens’ engagement in Goaso at the end of his two-day Resetting Ghana Tour of the Ahafo Region. He said the initiative would be replicated annually if the pilot project proved successful. President Mahama said the allocation from the District Assemblies Common Fund (DACF) for persons with disabilities had been increased from three per cent to five per cent under his administration. He also announced that the Persons with Disability Act, 2006 (Act 715), which seeks to protect and promote the rights of persons with disabilities, would be amended as part of efforts to improve their living conditions. On health, President Mahama said the government had implemented the Free Primary Healthcare Programme to provide free healthcare services to the public. He added that the Ghana Medical Trust Fund, also known as MahamaCares, had been established to reduce the financial burden of treating chronic diseases, including cancers and kidney disease requiring dialysis.

items.title: Bayern Munich : Ismaël Saibari encore décisif avec un but face à Augsbourg
items.description: Titulaire au poste de numéro 10 face à Augsbourg, Ismaël Saibari a une nouvelle fois marqué les esprits sous le maillot du Bayern Munich. L’international marocain a inscrit le but de l’égalisation (1-1), avant que le Bayern ne concède finalement le nul (2-2) dans un derby bavarois spectaculaire. Ismaël Saibari continue de gagner en importance au Bayern Munich. Aligné d’entrée samedi face à Augsbourg, l’international marocain a été titularisé dans un rôle de numéro 10, derrière Harry Kane et entre Michael Olise et Luis Díaz. Le Marocain s’est rapidement illustré dans une rencontre pourtant mal engagée pour le Bayern. Alors que Manuel Neuer avait offert un but précoce à Augsbourg après seulement six secondes de jeu, Saibari a eu l’occasion de remettre les siens sur les rails avant la pause, mais son face-à-face avec Finn Dahmen s’est soldé par une frappe à côté. Saibari n’a toutefois pas tardé à se rattraper. Quelques minutes après le but refusé à Luis Díaz par la VAR pour une position de hors-jeu, Harry Kane a trouvé le Marocain dans la surface. Ismael Saibari equalizes score. Assist by Harry Kane. Augsburg 1-1 Bayern Münich pic.twitter.com/tf5urAo1zY — Goals Xtra (@GoalsXtra) October 10, 2026 Un but important qui a permis au Bayern de revenir à 1-1 et de reprendre progressivement le contrôle de la rencontre. Le Marocain a ainsi confirmé son efficacité dans un rôle offensif plus axial, lui qui peut également évoluer dans différentes positions du secteur offensif. Le Bayern a finalement dû se contenter d’un match nul 2-2, après avoir été mené à deux reprises. Cette perte de points permet à Dortmund, également tenu en échec vendredi (2-2), de conserver deux longueurs d’avance en tête. The post Bayern Munich : Ismaël Saibari encore décisif avec un but face à Augsbourg appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: India's Cockroach Janta Party says thousands detained during New Delhi protest against CEC
items.description: Indian police detained the head of the Cockroach Janta Party , as well as thousands of protesters trying to take part in a major demonstration in New Delhi against the country’s election commissioner, the group said on Saturday. The protest is the culmination of weeks of opposition mobilisation following allegations of misconduct during a nationwide voter-roll revision by the Election Commission of India (ECI). CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other leaders were detained before disembarking from a flight in the capital, according to a statement from the movement. “They’re being denied access to their lawyers and cut off from all contact with others,” it said, adding the trio had been taken to “an undisclosed location”. The CJP also said that thousands more protesters were detained in New Delhi as they attempted to march to the main Jantar Mantar protest site, defying a massive security clampdown. “More than 15,000 protesters have been detained,” Ajinkya Shinde, a CJP leader, said at a news conference in Delhi. Police did not immediately respond to AFP ’s request for comment on detentions. “We will be back, let them fill up all the jails,” Shinde said. Dozens of protesters shouted anti-government slogans as they were taken away in police vehicles, AFP reporters witnessed. Calls for the ECI chief Gyanesh Kumar to step down have intensified in recent weeks as opposition parties and critics said his commission’s voter-roll revision could disenfranchise millions of constituents and benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The ECI has rejected allegations of impropriety, saying the revision was intended to remove duplicate and ineligible voters. Ahead of the protest, authorities in the capital deployed thousands of police, closed dozens of metro stations, cancelled more than 200 trains and temporarily shut down mobile internet around the protest site. Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel stand guard ahead of a protest by the youth-led Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) demanding the resignation of India’s Chief Election Commissioner over alleged “special intensive revision” (SIR) voter-roll irregularities, in New Delhi on October 10, 2026. — AFP The demonstrations are widely seen as a reprise of the “cockroach” movement’s mass mobilisation in July, which led to the education minister stepping down over an examination scandal. This time, protesters are demanding Kumar’s resignation and a halt to the voter revision exercise. Fresh challenge The accusations are a fresh challenge for 76-year-old Modi during his third term in office. Opposition parties have long alleged that legitimate voters are being struck off lists in India, the world’s largest democracy with 1.4 billion people. The issue flared up last month when Indian Express reported that key decisions linked to the revision were likely taken without the approval of two of the three election commissioners. The ECI, a constitutional body, says all its decisions were unanimous and legally valid. Demonstrators expressed anger on Saturday, telling AFP their right to protest peacefully was being hampered. Saransh, a university graduate, walked several miles after navigating security barricades to get close to the Jantar Mantar protest site. “I am here to protect the constitution,” said the 24-year-old, who gave only one name. “Why do I need permission to peacefully express my opinion?” ‘Keep protesting’ Amnesty International denounced the “lockdown-like restrictions” and leader of the opposition Congress party, Rahul Gandhi, called on young people to continue with the rallies. “Youth of India, I am proud of you. Keep protesting. We are standing with you,” he said. The Hindu reported that more than 5,000 protesters had been detained, although it was not immediately possible to verify that number. Media outlets, including the Scroll and Newslaundry , said their journalists had also been detained briefly. The United Nations’ human rights office urged India to release those “arbitrarily detained” in the protests and expressed concern at reports of mass detentions. BJP spokesman Sambit Patra said on Saturday the CJP had failed in its attempt to spread “anarchy”. “What is happening at Jantar Mantar, what you can see on TV and a few social media handles, is not India’s story,” he told reporters. The voter list overhaul, which began in 2025, has led to more than 133 million names being excluded from draft rolls, according to Indian media reports citing ECI data. The ECI has said the voter-roll revision identifies fraudulently registered voters and aims to prevent “foreign illegal immigrants” from voting. Critics say the drive has disproportionately affected marginalised and minority communities. Members of Modi’s party have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighbouring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India’s electoral rolls. Political analyst Nilanjan Mukhopadhyay told AFP the protest comes at a time when Modi appears to be “at his weakest politically and individually”. Though India’s next general elections are not slated until 2029, the country’s most populous state of Uttar Pradesh will go to the polls next year. “I see this becoming a bigger challenge in the coming months,” Mukhopadhyay said.

items.title: Army, Police dismiss report of 111 deaths in alleged Sokoto attack
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Army and the Sokoto State Police Command have debunked a viral social media post claiming that more than 100 civilians, 10 soldiers and a Mobile Police officer were killed in an alleged attack on a community in Sokoto State. The claim, published by a Facebook page (Hausaland Magazine) on October 5, 2026, alleged that armed men attacked a community identified as “Garin Gobir Gindin,” killing more than 100 civilians and security personnel, while kidnapping several others. The post, which described the alleged incident as a “genocide” and a “war on Hausa,” attributed the attack to “Fulani terrorists” and claimed that the death toll was rising. The viral post included an image showing several motionless individuals, some dressed in military-style clothing and others in civilian attire. It also attracted comments from social media users who appeared to accept and amplify the allegations, with some making inflammatory statements targeting ethnic groups. However, security authorities have denied that any such attack occurred in the state as there was no record of a community known as “Garin Gobir Gindin.” Investigation identified a date discrepancy in the post while the publication claimed the attack occurred on Tuesday, October 5, 2026, that date fell on a Monday. Acting Deputy Director, Army Public Relations, 8 Division, Nigerian Army, Lieutenant Colonel Olaniyi Osoba, dismissed the allegation, saying, “There was no such attack involving the reported mass casualties in the state. The Public Relations Officer of the Sokoto State Police Command, Deputy Superintendent of Police Ahmed Rufa’i, debunked the claim, saying, “This incident did not occur within Sokoto.” Verified security reports across the North-West also found no mass-casualty incident matching the description circulated by Hausaland Magazine. Investigations, however, identified a separate attack on Sunday, October 4, 2026, in Ungushi village, Kebbe Local Government Area of Sokoto State, where bandits reportedly killed two people and injured another. items.title: KGL U17 Colts 2026: Western beat Prempeh Elite Academy to set up final final with Greater Accra Region
items.description: Western Region delivered a composed and disciplined performance to eliminate Prempeh Elite Academy on penalties and secure a place in the final of the 2026 KGL Foundation Inter-Regional U17 Colts Championship at the Ghanaman Soccer Centre of Excellence on Saturday, October 10. The first semi-final ended in a pulsating 1-1 draw after 80 minutes of regulation time, forcing the contest to be decided from the penalty spot. Western Region appeared to have done enough to secure victory after Emmanuel Nyankumi fired them ahead in the 44th minute. However, Prempeh Elite Academy refused to surrender, with Thomas Asante striking two minutes from the end of regulation time to restore parity and breathe new life into the contest. With neither side able to find a decisive goal, the semi-final went to a penalty shootout, where Western Region held their nerve to claim a 4-2 victory and book their place in Sunday’s final. The result marked a significant achievement for Western Region, who produced a disciplined display to overcome one of the championship’s most impressive and free-scoring sides. Their reward is a place in the title decider, scheduled for Sunday, October 11, 2026, at the same venue. Western Region will face Greater Accra, who defeated Brong Ahafo Region, for the championship crown. The defeat brings Prempeh Elite Academy’s impressive campaign to an end and leaves them to contest third place after narrowly missing out on a place in the final. Sponsored by the KGL Foundation, the Inter-Regional U17 Colts Championship forms part of the Ghana Football Association’s Talent Development Scheme (TDS), which is dedicated to identifying, developing and nurturing the next generation of Ghanaian football talent. The competition provides promising under-17 players with a valuable platform to showcase their technical ability, tactical awareness and potential while gaining vital competitive experience against some of the country’s finest emerging talents.

items.title: Gaza : Médecins du Monde affirme que les critères du génocide sont réunis
items.description: L'agression israélienne contre la bande de Gaza a fait près de 75 000 morts depuis octobre 2023. Alors qu’Israël et son gouvernement extrémistes comptent encore des défenseurs, de plus en plus d’ONG et de personnalités internationales n'hésitent plus à qualifier ce qui se passe dans l’enclave palestinienne de génocide. Les critères de définition d’un tel crime ont été retrouvés sur le terrain, assure l’ONG Médecins du Monde. S'exprimant sur Arte, Jean-François Corty, président de l’ONG, a expliqué que le génocide “ n'est pas un ressenti ” ou “ une opinion ” mais “ une définition juridique qui renvoie à des déterminants précis ”. Dans ces déterminants, a-t-il poursuivi, « le nombre de morts n'est pas un indicateur, rappelant à titre d’exemple que les 37 000 morts de Srebrenica et les 800 000 morts du Rwanda, ont été caractérisés comme des génocides malgré l'écart entre le nombre des victimes ». Médecins du Monde : des critères du génocide retrouvés sur le terrain à Gaza À Gaza , a-t-il assuré, « il y a des critères qui ont été retrouvés par son équipe sur le terrain, par Human Rights Watch, par MSF (Médecins sans frontières), par des enquêtes indépendantes des Nations-Unies … » Il y a, a égrené le président de Médecins du Monde, une volonté de “ rendre les conditions de vie insupportables avec un impact psychologique et physique sur les populations, une aide qui est empêchée de rentrer d’une manière proportionnée, un impact sur les taux de natalité… ” Le tout se fait dans un contexte “ de conditionnalité et d'intentionnalité énoncée ”. “ Les autorités israéliennes, de nombreux acteurs ont énoncé la volonté de tuer tout ou partie. La définition d’un génocide c’est tuer tout ou partie d’une population ”, a rappelé Jean-François Corty. “ Donc ces déterminants sont en faveur d’un génocide ”, a-t-il conclu. #gaza Un génocide en cours, pour de vrai. https://t.co/mF9cG6flhT — Jean-françois Corty (@JfCorty) October 8, 2026 L’article Gaza : Médecins du Monde affirme que les critères du génocide sont réunis est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Ibrahima Khalil Diallo invité officiellement par le gouvernement polonais : une nouvelle étape dans son parcours politique
items.description: L’acteur politique guinéen Ibrahima Khalil Diallo, membre du Bureau exécutif national du Parti MODEL, prendra part à un programme d’études à Varsovie, en Pologne, à l’invitation officielle du gouvernement polonais. Destiné aux jeunes leaders africains et internationaux, ce programme constitue une opportunité d’approfondir la connaissance des réalités politiques, économiques et institutionnelles de la Pologne, tout en explorant les perspectives de coopération avec l’Union européenne. Pour Ibrahima Khalil Diallo, cette invitation représente bien plus qu’un déplacement d’études : elle s’inscrit dans une dynamique de formation, d’ouverture internationale et de consolidation de son engagement politique. Les échanges prévus permettront notamment de mieux appréhender les modèles de gouvernance, les dynamiques économiques et les enjeux stratégiques qui façonnent la Pologne et l’espace européen. Engagé en faveur d’une Guinée démocratique, apaisée et résolument tournée vers l’avenir, le jeune acteur politique entend tirer profit de cette expérience pour enrichir sa réflexion et renforcer sa capacité à contribuer au débat public national. Il considère cette opportunité comme une invitation à apprendre, à confronter les expériences et à consolider ses convictions au contact d’autres parcours de leadership. À l’heure où la Guinée aspire à renouveler ses pratiques politiques et à renforcer ses perspectives de développement, cette expérience internationale constitue une étape significative dans le parcours d’un acteur politique qui entend inscrire son engagement dans la durée, la compétence et l’ouverture sur le monde. items.title: Late Solanke strike salvages 10-man Spurs draw at Man United
items.description: Dominic Solanke scored in stoppage time to salvage a point for 10-man Tottenham as they snatched a draw against Manchester United in a feisty encounter at Old Trafford. It looked as if United were about to pile more misery on the visitors following their pitiful start to the Premier League season when Bryan Mbeumo broke the deadlock in the 73rd minute. Things went from bad to worse for Spurs when Rodrigo Bentancur was sent off five minutes later for headbutting Luke Shaw, who had shoved him over after a reckless challenge from the Uruguay midfielder. But Solanke, who was captaining Tottenham for the first time, nodded Sandro Tonali’s cross into the back of the net in the second minute of added time to lift Spurs off the bottom of the table. Roberto de Zerbi’s side remain winless, however, and stay in the relegation zone – above both Fulham and Coventry City – with just three points from the first six games. United have suffered their own shaky start to the campaign with just one victory and a sluggish first-half performance was met with boos by the home fans on Saturday. They were much improved after the break, but jeers once again echoed around Old Trafford at full-time. This was the second successive league game they have dropped points against a team that were reduced to 10 men – following their 1-0 derby defeat by Manchester City last month.

items.title: Gender Ministry to monitor welfare of Nana Akua Addo’s children amid domestic violence case
items.description: The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection says it will deploy social welfare officers to monitor the welfare of the children of Ghanaian fashion personality Nana Akua Addo and her husband, Harold Norman, amid a domestic violence case involving the family. The decision follows a meeting between the Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection, Dr Agnes Naa Momo Lartey, and Mr Norman after his discharge from hospital. Dr Lartey had earlier visited the family and interacted with Nana Akua Addo. However, Mr Norman was unavailable at the time as he was receiving medical care. During her subsequent engagement with Mr Norman, the Minister emphasised the need to protect the children from conflict and situations that could compromise their safety, emotional wellbeing and development. The Ministry said social welfare officers would monitor the children’s welfare to help safeguard their interests and ensure their safety remains a priority. It added that it would continue collaborating with the Police and other relevant institutions to support the family while investigations into the domestic violence case continue.

items.title: INEC drops Pantami from final list of Gombe governorship candidates
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has dropped the name of former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Prof. Isa Ali Ibrahim Pantami, from the final list of governorship candidates for Gombe State. Pantami, who appeared on the provisional list published on August 29, is conspicuously missing from the final list published in Saturday night. He emerged as the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate after dumping the All Progressives Congress (APC) on May 19. Ahmed Mailantarki Mailantarki, one of the aspirants who sought the PDP ticket, challenged Pantami’s victory in court. A Federal High Court sitting in Gombe nullified the election and ordered a fresh primary, which Pantami won again. His biggest obstacle, however, was the September 24 Supreme Court judgement, which restored Sections 77(5), (6), (7) and 84(2) of the Electoral Act 2026. The provisions bar parties from fielding candidates whose names were not in the membership register submitted to INEC within the stipulated time. A total of 16 candidates were cleared to contest the February 6, 2027 governorship election in the state. They include Bala Bello Tinka of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Jamilu Isyaku Gwamna of the APC and Babayo Ardo Kumo of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC). Others are Zubairu Mu’azu Halilu of the Labour Party, Lamela L. Silas of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Ibrahim Jalo Abubakar of the People’s Redemption Party (PRP) and Adamu Mohammed Ma’aji of the Social Democratic Party (SDP). Uncertainty had trailed Pantami’s participation in the election. Mohammed Haruna, an INEC National Commissioner, had hinted on Trust TV’s Daily Politics that, in line with the Supreme Court ruling, some parties would not field candidates in 2027. The post INEC drops Pantami from final list of Gombe governorship candidates appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Michael Jackson version symphonique | L’évènement musical à ne pas manquer à la Cité de la Culture
items.description: Trente ans après le concert historique du King of Pop à Tunis, l’Orchestre symphonique tunisien, sous la direction de Shady Garfi, ressuscite la magie de Michael Jackson le jeudi 29 octobre 2026 à l’Opéra de Tunis. Un spectacle symphonique inédit mêlant musique, chant et danse pour faire revivre les plus grands tubes de la légende pop sera ainsi donné au Théâtre de l’Opéra de Tunis de la Cité de la Culture Chedly Klibi, le jeudi 29 octobre 2026. A l’initiative et sous la direction de son chef, Shady Garfi, l’Orchestre symphonique tunisien est en train de vous préparer quelque chose d’ENORME : Un concert Tribute to Mickael Jackson ! Oui ! vous avez bien lu, bien entendu ! 30 après son passage pareil à celui d’une étoile filante, on fait ressusciter la légende du King of pop et cette magie qui traverse les frontières et les générations !! Trente ans déjà ! Le 7 octobre 1996, Michael Jackson faisait vibrer Tunis lors de son inoubliable concert au stade olympique d’El Menzah. Un événement historique, des milliers de fans en folie et des souvenirs qui, trois décennies plus tard, n’ont pas pris une ride. Le King of Pop a beau nous avoir quittés, sa musique, elle, n’a jamais cessé de danser ! En évocation de cet anniversaire symbolique, l’Orchestre symphonique tunisien vous donne rendez-vous avec un spectacle unique : Tribute to Michael Jackson , une célébration toute en rythme et en émotions, baignée du goût doux-amer de la nostalgie, conçue par le dynamique chef Shady Garfi et produite par le Théâtre de l’Opéra de Tunis – Pôle Musique et Opéra. Au programme : les plus grands tubes du King of Pop revisités par les sonorités puissantes d’un orchestre symphonique, avec chant et danse pour faire monter la température et amplifier le plaisir! De Billie Jean à Thriller, de Beat It à Smooth Criminal, préparez-vous à retrouver ces mélodies mythiques gravées dans la mémoire des générations et font l’effet d’un courant électrique qui fait automatiquement bouger, danser les corps, touts âges confondus. Et pour que la soirée soit au top, de jeunes et nouvelles voix tunisiennes seront de la partie pour interpréter les lyrics. Vous aurez donc le plaisir de découvrir Daly Mj, Rabaa Ammar, Farah Zribi Une intention que Michael Jackson aurait sans doute adorée ! Faire dialoguer la magie de la musique symphonique avec son irrésistible énergie, dans un spectacle où les cordes rencontrent le groove, où les grandes envolées orchestrales côtoient les rythmes légendaires et où la danse promet de faire revivre l’esprit du King. Que vous ayez vécu le concert de 1996 ou que vous ayez découvert Michael Jackson sur YouTube, dans les playlists de vos parents ou grâce à TikTok, une chose est sûre : son univers appartient au monde entier, faisant fi de toutes les frontières. Les fans de la première heure retrouveront leurs classiques, tandis que les plus jeunes pourront découvrir, en live et en grand format, pourquoi Michael reste cette légende absolue de la pop. Trente ans après El Menzah, l’histoire continue. Cette fois, pas besoin de remonter le temps: il suffit de se laisser emporter par la musique, de suivre le rythme et, qui sait, de tenter quelques pas de Moonwalk en sortant ! Alors, venez vite, venez vite, on vous invite, on vous attend ! items.title: « Le Président de la République est en train de faire assez de choses pour le peuple de Guinée et compte beaucoup sur la justice pour l’accompagner… » (ministre)
items.description: En mission de travail à Kankan, le Garde des Sceaux, Ministre de la Justice et des Droits de l’Homme, Ibrahima Sory II Tounkara, a appelé l’institution judiciaire à accompagner l’action du Président de la République, le Général Mamadi Doumbouya. S’exprimant devant les responsables judiciaires de la ville, le ministre a insisté sur le rôle central que doit jouer la justice dans la dynamique impulsée par le Chef de l’État en faveur de la population guinéenne. « Aujourd’hui, M. le Président de la République est en train de faire assez de choses pour le peuple de Guinée et compte beaucoup sur la justice pour l’accompagner dans cette œuvre », a déclaré le Garde des Sceaux. Pour Ibrahima Sory II Tounkara, le Chef de l’État agit dans l’intérêt supérieur de la nation et l’appareil judiciaire se doit de contribuer à cette œuvre, dans le strict respect des textes en vigueur. « Et la justice doit l’accompagner, parce que voilà quelqu’un qui veut du bien pour ce peuple », a-t-il poursuivi. Le ministre a ensuite mis un accent particulier sur la responsabilité des magistrats dans le rendu de leurs décisions. Il a appelé à une justice rendue conformément aux lois de la République. « Il faudrait que la justice l’accompagne en rendant de très bonnes décisions, en faisant normalement l’effet conformément aux lois de la République », a-t-il martelé. S’adressant directement au Procureur de la République près le Tribunal de première instance de Kankan, le Garde des Sceaux a conclu par un appel à la vigilance. « Vous devez veiller au sein de ce tribunal, vous, monsieur le procureur de la République. Je compte sur vous pour le faire. » Par cette déclaration, le ministère de la Justice entend réaffirmer le rôle de soutien que doit jouer l’institution judiciaire dans l’action publique, tout en rappelant l’exigence fondamentale du respect de la loi dans le traitement des dossiers. Karifa Kansan Doumbouya, correspondant régional – Kankan L’article « Le Président de la République est en train de faire assez de choses pour le peuple de Guinée et compte beaucoup sur la justice pour l’accompagner… » (ministre) est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Benedict Okyere Yeboah: Ghana’s football problem goes beyond sacking a coach
items.description: Sacking the coach is the easiest answer to Ghana’s football problems. It is also unlikely to be the solution. Carlos Queiroz has now left his position after Ghana opened the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign with defeats to Côte d’Ivoire and The Gambia. His seven-match spell produced one win, one draw and five defeats. Those numbers are poor. They justify serious questions about the coaching period. But they should not end the conversation. Because Ghana’s decline did not begin with Queiroz. The evidence points to a deeper problem. Ghana failed to qualify for AFCON 2025 after a qualifying campaign in which the Black Stars recorded three draws and three defeats, scoring only three goals in six matches and conceding seven. That was before Queiroz’s second spell. At AFCON 2023, Ghana managed only two points from three group matches, failed to win a game and conceded six goals. The pattern therefore stretches across different competitions and coaching periods. Changing the manager repeatedly may change the tactics. It does not automatically change the football ecosystem producing the players, developing the clubs or preparing the national teams. How many coaches do we need to change before we change the system? Ghana has increasingly treated the national team coach as the central explanation for every failure. But if different coaches inherit similar structural problems, eventually the question has to move beyond the dugout. The Black Stars have experienced repeated coaching changes in recent years, while the underlying concerns around player development, club sustainability, infrastructure and football administration have remained. The GFA itself acknowledged the seriousness of the problem after the AFCON 2025 failure. In November 2024, it dissolved the Black Stars Management Committee and announced a Ghana Football Retreat involving stakeholders from football, government, education, finance, economics, marketing, former players and other sectors. The stated objective was to develop a roadmap for improving Ghana football. That is significant. It means the problem was already being recognised as bigger than the head coach. The local league is part of the national team equation. A national team cannot permanently operate as an island. The domestic football system is supposed to develop players, coaches, referees, administrators and clubs capable of feeding the national teams. Yet in March 2026, the GFA’s Club Licensing Manager said that among the 18 Ghana Premier League clubs, only seven owned their own facilities and only four owned their own stadia. That is a structural issue. If elite clubs lack adequate infrastructure and sustainable commercial foundations, the national team cannot simply be expected to produce a continuous pipeline of elite players. The government’s 2026–2029 Medium-Term Development Plan also identifies inadequate sports infrastructure in schools as a problem for early talent identification and systematic athlete development. So the question is not simply: “Who should coach the Black Stars?” It is also: “Where are we developing the next generation of Black Stars?” Ghana has talent — but talent is not a development system. This is perhaps the most important distinction. Ghana continues to produce talented footballers. Mohammed Kudus, Thomas Partey, Antoine Semenyo and numerous other Ghanaian players demonstrate that the talent pool has not disappeared. The problem is whether Ghana consistently converts that talent into a strong national football system. Interestingly, the GFA announced in August 2026 that it had invested GH¢1.8 million to train 600 Colts coaches through its CAF Licence D programme over two seasons. It also announced continued investment in youth competitions, equipment and regional development. Those investments matter. But they also highlight the scale of the challenge. If grassroots coaching, facilities, scouting, competitions and player pathways are weak or inconsistent, improving one national-team camp will not fix the entire production line. Money alone is not enough either The GFA announced that every Ghana Premier League club would receive at least GH¢1 million ahead of the 2025/26 season, alongside equipment and logistical support. That raises another important question: What does the money build? Does it create better academies? Better pitches? Professional commercial departments? Improved scouting? Youth development programmes? Medical and sports-science structures? Or does it simply help clubs survive another season? Ghana’s Sports Minister Kofi Iddie Adams raised essentially this issue in August 2026, arguing that football requires rebuilding from grassroots to the national level and questioning whether financial interventions were producing lasting institutional improvements. That is where the conversation needs to go. The Black Stars are a symptom, not the entire disease. Consider the numbers. AFCON 2023: 3 matches — 0 wins — 2 draws — 1 defeat — 5 goals scored — 6 conceded. AFCON 2025 qualifying: 6 matches — 0 wins — 3 draws — 3 defeats — 3 goals scored — 7 conceded. Queiroz’s 2026 spell: 7 matches — 1 win — 1 draw — 5 defeats. These numbers cannot simply be explained by one tactical system. They represent a longer period of instability. And that is why Ghana’s next coaching appointment should be viewed as one component of a much larger football reform programme. What actually needs fixing? Ghana needs to examine the entire football pyramid: Grassroots development Identify talent earlier and create structured pathways from schools and Colts football into professional academies. Club development Clubs need stronger ownership models, academies, facilities, commercial departments and revenue streams. Coaching development The country needs more high-level coaches at youth and senior levels — not just a succession of expensive solutions for the Black Stars. Scouting Ghana must build a modern national scouting network capable of identifying talent domestically and across the diaspora. Infrastructure Training pitches, academies, medical facilities and performance centres cannot remain secondary issues. National-team continuity The Black Stars need a football philosophy that survives individual coaching changes. Accountability Success should be measured not only by whether Ghana qualifies for the next tournament, but by whether the football system is becoming stronger. The uncomfortable truth Ghana can sack Queiroz. It can appoint another coach. It can change the technical team. It can even change the Black Stars management committee. But if the same weaknesses remain underneath, the cycle simply starts again. A new coach can improve a team. A new football structure can improve a country. That distinction matters. The Black Stars’ recent numbers are serious enough to demand action. But the statistics also tell us something else: the problem has lasted longer than any single coach. Ghana therefore needs more than another coaching appointment. It needs a football development strategy that connects schools, Colts football, academies, clubs, the Ghana Premier League, the diaspora and the national teams into one functioning pathway. Because if Ghana only changes the man on the touchline, it may change the face of the problem without changing the system producing it. The next coach should not be expected to rescue Ghanaian football alone. That job belongs to the entire football system.

items.title: Justice Francis Korbieh: How a boy from the village became a Court of Appeal judge and not a priest
items.description: “I didn’t get the calling. So that’s why I didn’t become a priest.” That was how retired Court of Appeal judge Justice Francis Gyafiiry Korbieh explained, with laughter, why he did not follow the path to priesthood despite attending a seminary established to train Catholic priests and young men for Christian life. Instead, he went on to become a lawyer, parliamentarian and judge, building a career spanning five decades in Ghana’s legal profession. But the journey began far from the courtroom, in a village in the Upper West Region where access to education demanded long walks and considerable determination. Speaking on Joy FM’s Personality Profile with Lexis Bill on Thursday, October 8, Justice Korbieh recalled how he had to walk about 10 miles from his village to attend primary school because there was no school in the community. “Well, let me start by saying that I come from a village that is uh 10 miles due east of Jirapa,” he said. “There was no school there. So I had to walk those 10 miles, let me say 10 kilometers.” His school operated a boarding system, allowing pupils to remain on campus during the week. But getting there and returning home was still a demanding routine. “I used to walk to the school, attend school for one week, walk back to my village for two days and then walk back to school for another week”. The journey continued throughout his six years of primary education, a routine that offered an early lesson in perseverance. His circumstances changed in Primary Six when he gained admission to St Francis Xavier Minor Seminary, a new secondary school established in the then diocese of Wa. It was an unusual development for a child from his part of the country, where, according to him, proceeding directly from Primary Six to secondary school was then uncommon. “It was a novelty at the time because in our part of the country, nobody ever went to secondary school from Primary Six.” The school had been established by the late Cardinal Peter Porekuu Dery, who was then Bishop of Wa. Justice Korbieh was among its pioneer students. He said the school initially operated in Jirapa before relocating to Wa after its first term. A seminary, but not a priest St Francis Xavier Minor Seminary was established with two objectives: to prepare young men for the priesthood and to educate those who would pursue other careers while serving God and the country. For Korbieh, the second path was the one he chose. When asked whether he had wanted to become a priest, he responded candidly: “I didn’t want to become a priest.” He then offered a light-hearted explanation for the decision. “A priest? I didn’t get the calling. So that’s why I didn’t become a priest.” Although he did not enter the priesthood, Korbieh said his life had remained connected to both public service and the church. “But here I am. I serve my country very well. I also serve the church very well” Five decades in the legal profession Korbieh’s journey eventually took him from the classroom into legal practice, Parliament and the judiciary. Born on 20 December 1950 at Jirapa/Kuncheni, Justice Korbieh pursued further studies at St. Peter’s Secondary School, the University of Ghana, and the Ghana School of Law. He was called to the Ghana Bar on 30 September 1976, marking five decades in the legal fraternity this year. He went on to serve as the Member of Parliament for Jirapa from 1993 to 2001 before elevating to the Bench, where he served as a Justice of the Court of Appeal until his retirement in 2020. Yet, for the retired judge, the foundation of every judgment written and every law passed remains those 10 long miles walked in pursuit of a dream.

items.title: GPL 2026/27: Darkwah Wiafe’s winner sees All Blacks beat Kotoko
items.description: Asante Kotoko suffered defeat on matchday six of the Ghana Premier League (GPL) following their loss to Swedru All Blacks. The two teams faced off on Saturday, October 10, with Asante Kotoko hoping to make it two wins out of two since the departure of Eric Tinkler. However, All Blacks condemned them to their second defeat of the camp, as they claimed a 1-0 win at home. The Porcupine Warriors came into the fixture on the back of a narrow win over Karela United in their last game, while All Blacks came into this game having lost to Aduana Football Club in their last league outing. Despite a confident start to the game in Swedru, Kotoko created very few chances but were kept in the game by their goalkeeper, who made numerous saves to keep out the threat of the home side, heading into the break at 0-0. The return from recess saw a similar style, with All Blacks throwing everything at Kotoko, but once again Aziz Dari was on hand to keep his side in the game. When it looked as if the Kumasi-based side were going to leave Swedru with a point, they conceded a penalty. The penalty was converted by Darkwah Wiafe to give All Blacks all three points and move them to eight points after six games played. They also go level with Kotoko who now have two wins, two draws and two defeats from six games so far this season.

items.title: Ghana must pursue BRICS partnership if it brings economic benefits – Kpebu
items.description: Legal practitioner and analyst Martin Kpebu says Ghana should pursue a partnership with the BRICS economic bloc if it offers tangible economic benefits to the country. He argues that Ghana’s foreign policy should be guided by national interest rather than an exclusive alignment with traditional Western partners. Speaking on TV3’s The Key Points, Mr Kpebu said the country must be willing to explore opportunities with different international partners, just as major global powers pursue relationships based on their own interests. “I support Ghana becoming a partner, as long as it brings us economic development. We don’t have much so if there is something to be gained from it, why not?” he said. His comments come after Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa announced that the government had decided to formally apply for Ghana to join BRICS. The government says the move is intended to diversify Ghana’s international partnerships, expand economic opportunities and strengthen cooperation with countries in the Global South. Mr Kpebu dismissed concerns that Ghana’s engagement with BRICS would automatically undermine its longstanding relationship with the United States. He noted that Ghana and the US have maintained diplomatic and economic ties over several decades, arguing that those relationships would not necessarily collapse because Ghana sought cooperation with other economic blocs. “The U.S. is not going to run out of Ghana overnight because we join BRICS,” he said. According to him, Ghana’s engagement with alternative economic partners could also encourage traditional allies to attach greater value to their relationship with the country. He argued that international relations are driven largely by national interest, and Ghana should adopt a similar approach in determining its partnerships. “What do we gain by continuing to say, ‘Oh, we are with the U.S., we are with the UK, so we can’t join BRICS?’” he asked. Mr Kpebu further compared international relations to competition for attention, suggesting that Ghana’s willingness to explore other partnerships could strengthen its position in dealings with existing allies. He clarified that his support was for Ghana pursuing partner status with BRICS rather than necessarily seeking full membership immediately. “ As long as we’re going to get benefits, let’s go for it,” he said. BRICS, originally formed by Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, has expanded to include additional members. The grouping seeks to strengthen economic cooperation and increase the influence of emerging economies in global affairs. Mr Kpebu’s comments add to the debate over how Ghana can pursue new economic opportunities while managing its existing diplomatic relationships.

items.title: Success and Wright Claims J100 Accra Girls’ Doubles Championship
items.description: Success Ogunjobi of Nigeria and Sydney Wright of the United States were crowned Girls’ Doubles champions at the J100 Accra, Tennis Foundation Ghana Open . Sydney Wright and Success Ogunjobi defeated Poland’s Alisha Ndukwu and Russia’s Milana Kolesova 6-3, 6-1 in a dominant final display at the Accra Sports Stadium National Tennis Centre. Determined to complete a back-to-back title run, Wright set the tone alongside Ogunjobi with sharp communication and aggressive baseline play. The pair worked in flawless sync, refusing to allow their top-ranked opponents any margin for error. Success and Sydney started the match with total confidence dominating the opening set 6-3. Ogunjobi and Wright accelerated through the second set, dropping just one game to wrap up the championship match with clinical efficiency. Building on her doubles’ victory,Wright maintained her winning streak with to win the girls’ singles title. For Ogunjobi, lifting the trophy showcased her great skill, teamwork, and determination on the big stage. The tournament draws the curtain on a great six-week junior tour in Accra, marking the successful conclusion of the ninth edition of the ITF World Tennis Tour Juniors in Accra. A major tournament on the international junior calendar, the Tennis Foundation Ghana Open continues to serve as a vital pathway for high-performance for junior players striving to make their mark on the global stage.
